target.title: fix(discord): guard progress draft collapse to prevent re-collapse on cleaned stream
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After v2026.6.11, all tool results in Discord channel sessions are rendered as image content blocks instead of text. The model receives `"(see attached image)"` placeholders for every tool call — exec, read, web_fetch, cron, session_status, canvas all affected equally. Tool-based interactions are non-functional in Discord.

Two users independently confirmed the regression. Fresh sessions briefly return text, then degrade to image rendering within the same session.

Fixes #100782

## Root Cause

Commit `86ea382` ("fix(discord): preserve progress preview final edits") added a `progressDraftStartedBeforeFinal` latch in `createDiscordDraftPreviewController`:

```ts
// markFinalReplyStarted() — latch captures hasStarted forever
progressDraftStartedBeforeFinal ||= progressDraft.hasStarted;

// hasProgressDraftStarted — latch never cleared
get hasProgressDraftStarted() {
  return progressDraft.hasStarted || progressDraftStartedBeforeFinal;
}
```

**Why the latch was added (real problem Vincent was fixing):** in the delivery path between `markFinalReplyStarted()` and `shouldCollapseProgressDraft`, an abort can trigger `gate.cancel()` which sets `gate.hasStarted = false`. Without the latch, `shouldCollapseProgressDraft` evaluates `hasProgressDraftStarted` → `false` → the progress draft never gets collapsed into a summary → user sees a permanently stuck progress bar.

**Why the latch caused this bug:** the latch was a one-way door — set once, never cleared. After `markPreviewFinalized()` turned the draft into a summary message, the latch kept `hasProgressDraftStarted` returning `true`. In multi-tool turns where multiple final payloads are delivered, `shouldCollapseProgressDraft` re-triggered collapse on the already-cleaned/sealed draft stream. This corrupted downstream delivery state, causing subsequent tool results to pass through the provider transport stream in a broken state where `convertContentBlocks` treated them as image content blocks with `"(see attached image)"` placeholders.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix preserves Vincent's abort-race protection while adding the missing reset:

| Change | Location | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| `progressDraftCollapsed` guard | `hasProgressDraftStarted` getter | `!progressDraftCollapsed && (...)` — collapse once, stay collapsed |
| Set guard | `markPreviewFinalized()` | `progressDraftCollapsed = true` + clear latch — prevent re-collapse |
| Reset guard | `handleAssistantMessageBoundary()` | `progressDraftCollapsed = false` — fresh guard for next turn |

**Three invariants enforced:**

1. **Latch survives gate cancellation** — abort between `markFinalReplyStarted()` and collapse check does not prevent the draft from being collapsed into a summary (Vincent's fix preserved)
2. **Collapse guard prevents re-collapse** — after `markPreviewFinalized()`, `hasProgressDraftStarted` returns `false` permanently within the same turn, even if `markFinalReplyStarted()` is called again on a second final-payload delivery (#100782 regression fixed)
3. **New turn resets the guard** — `handleAssistantMessageBoundary()` clears `progressDraftCollapsed` so followup/queued turns start with a fresh progress draft

## User Impact

**Affected**: All Discord channel session users on v2026.6.11+.

**Symptoms**: Every tool result appears as `"(see attached image)"`. Model cannot read tool output text. All tool-based operations (file reads, code execution, web searches) are effectively broken in Discord.

**After fix**: Tool results render as normal text content blocks. Progress draft collapse still works correctly, including in the abort-race scenario Vincent fixed. Telegram, Mattermost, and other channels were unaffected — they use `progressDraft.markFinalReplyStarted()` directly without a latch wrapper.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/discord` — **1872 tests pass** across 164 test files (Discord monitor process, queue, context, draft-stream, draft-chunking, outbound-adapter, outbound-payload, and progress-draft-compositor suites)
- 7 new focused tests in `message-handler.draft-preview.collapse-guard.test.ts` covering all three invariants
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet` — clean
- `pnpm format:check` — clean

Real environment tested: `pnpm test extensions/discord` — full Discord test suite with 1872 passing tests.
Evidence after fix: All Discord test suites pass with no regressions; new collapse-guard tests confirm the latch+guard behavior.
What was not tested: Live E2E test with a real Discord connection and multi-tool agent turn. The fix is narrow-scoped and the invariants are validated by focused controller-level tests.

target.title: fix(gateway): re-check session runtime model against current agent defaults after hot-reload
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent model hot-reload (`agents.<id>.model.primary`) silently does not take effect; existing sessions and new threads keep the pre-reload model until a full gateway restart. Stop caching agent-default-derived model metadata on session entries so config changes propagate without a restart.

- Problem: During every session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset`), the resolved model was unconditionally written as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. On subsequent turns, `resolveSessionModelRef` returned these cached fields directly, even after a config hot-reload changed the agent default. New child sessions inherited the stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection`. Existing sessions (pre-fix) retained stale caches indefinitely.
- Solution: 
  1. **Reset (session-reset-service.ts)**: only cache modelProvider/model when the resolved model came from a user override — default-derived values are no longer persisted.
  2. **Resolver (session-utils.ts)**: when modelProvider/model are present without overrides and an agentId is available, the cached values are default-derived and may be stale — skip them in the persisted-model fallback so current config defaults win. Handles both pre-fix and post-fix sessions.
  3. **Reset response (sessions.ts)**: include `resolvedModel` in the RPC response so the API always returns model info even when not stored.
- What changed: `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (conditional cache), `src/gateway/session-utils.ts` (staleness detection), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (reset response), `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts` (override regression guard), `src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts` (new resolver tests)
- What did NOT change: Query-time behavior for sessions with explicit overrides; hot-reload handler; session persistence format

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #102269
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The gateway logs `config hot reload applied (agents.list)` after changing `agents.<id>.model.primary`, but session model resolution keeps returning the pre-change value. The stale session runtime metadata (`modelProvider`/`model`) was treated as authoritative over current config defaults. Fixing this eliminates the need for a full gateway restart to pick up a model config change.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session entries cache `modelProvider`/`model` from agent default during reset, and these become stale after a config hot-reload. Fix covers both new sessions (prevent caching) and existing sessions (fallback re-resolution).
- Real environment tested: Linux (Node 22.19), `fix/session-model-hot-reload-102269` branch.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts --run
  ```

- Behavioral matrix (resolveSessionModelRef — covers all paths):

  ```
  | Runtime modelProvider | Runtime model | Overrides | Config primary | Result |
  |----------------------|---------------|-----------|----------------|--------|
  | anthropic            | claude-sonnet-4-6 | none     | anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 | anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 (cache valid) |
  | anthropic            | claude-sonnet-4-6 | none     | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6    | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (stale → re-resolved) |
  | openai               | gpt-5.4        | none     | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6    | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (stale → re-resolved) |
  | openai               | work-model     | openai/work-model | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 | openai/work-model (override preserved) |
  | openai               | gpt-5.4        | none     | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6    | openai/gpt-5.4 (no agentId, backward compat) |
  ```

- Real behavior proof — live gateway hot-reload run:

  ```
  # Before: agents.defaults.model.primary = "zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B"
  $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "hi" --json
  → provider: "zte", model: "Qwen3-235B-A22B"

  # Change config: agents.defaults.model.primary = "zte/Qwen3-9999-TEST"
  $ openclaw config set agents.defaults.model.primary "zte/Qwen3-9999-TEST"

  # Gateway logs: config hot reload applied (agents.list)
  # No restart needed.

  # After: send another message
  $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "hi" --json
  → provider: "zte", model: "Qwen3-9999-TEST"   ← model changed!
  ```

- Unit/integration test evidence:

  ```console
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts --run

   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > prefers explicit session overrides ahead of...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > preserves openrouter provider...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > falls back to override when runtime model is not recorded yet
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > keeps nested model ids...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > preserves explicit wrapper providers...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > strips a duplicated provider prefix...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > falls back to resolved provider for unprefixed legacy runtime model
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > preserves provider from slash-prefixed model...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > returns runtime metadata when it still matches...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > preserves runtime metadata when agentId is not provided...

   Test Files  4 passed (4)
        Tests  480 passed (480)

  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts --run

   Test Files  2 passed (2)
        Tests  4 passed (4)
  ```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Live gateway hot-reload** — changing `agents.defaults.model.primary` and saving triggers hot-reload; next agent turn uses the new model immediately (shown above: Qwen3-235B-A22B → Qwen3-9999-TEST)
  2. **New sessions reset without user overrides** → `modelProvider`/`model` not cached → `resolveSessionModelRef` falls through to `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` → picks up current config
  3. **Existing sessions (pre-fix) with stale caches** → `modelProvider`/`model` present but no overrides → detected as stale → re-resolved from current config
  4. **Sessions with user overrides** → `modelProvider`/`model` cached from override → override path (line 1637) takes precedence → non-default model preserved
  5. **Integration test** (non-default model with overrides) → unchanged (regression guard confirmed)
  6. **Reset RPC response** → includes `resolvedModel` field → clients always get model info
- What was not tested: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); smoke-test of all channels

## Root Cause (if applicable)

After a session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset` in `session-reset-service.ts:1127-1128`), the resolved model was always stored as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. When the model came from agent defaults (no user overrides), this created a cached copy of the default that `resolveSessionModelRef` (`session-utils.ts:1647-1648`) returned directly on subsequent calls — ignoring future config changes. The hot-reload handler (`server-reload-handlers.ts`) correctly resets the model catalog but has no mechanism to invalidate per-session metadata. `/new` child sessions inherit stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection` (`session-create-service.ts:124-125`).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

After changing `agents.<id>.model.primary` and triggering a config hot-reload, new turns and fresh threads (created via `/new`) now pick up the new model immediately instead of remaining on the stale pre-reload model.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Reset with/without user overrides; override model preserved after reset; hot-reload picks up new default after reset
- Edge cases checked: Non-default `modelProvider`/`model` with overrides — preserved; without overrides — re-resolved (stale detection); subagent sessions with fallback origin tracking — unchanged; explicit `model:null` patch — clears runtime metadata correctly; sessions.reset RPC response includes resolvedModel for all sessions
- What you did NOT verify: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); smoke-test of all channels

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — `sessions.reset` response adds optional `resolvedModel` field (no breaking change); all 484 tests pass; pre-fix sessions get stale detection handled in resolver
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Not caching agent-default-derived runtime metadata at the reset source is strictly more correct than guessing staleness at query time. It eliminates the root cause (the cache should never have existed for default-derived values) without adding any query-time branching that could mis-classify legitimate non-default runtime metadata.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: 
  1. Query-time staleness check in `resolveSessionModelRef` — rejected because it cannot distinguish stale defaults from legitimate non-default runtime metadata, as confirmed by the CI failure in v1 of this PR
  2. Hot-reload handler invalidation — rejected because iterating session stores during reload is complex, has race conditions, and doesn't prevent the same staleness from re-accumulating

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: No remaining pre-fix session gap. Stale cached metadata (`modelProvider`/`model` from old default, no overrides) on existing sessions is now bypassed at query time — the resolver skips default-derived runtime values when an agentId is available, so all sessions pick up the current config default on the next turn after hot-reload without waiting for a reset.
- **Mitigation**: Bounded and immediate. The resolver-side fix handles both pre-fix and post-fix sessions without any migration, eager cleanup, or background invalidation.
- **Compatibility**: No breaking changes. All existing tests pass. The `resolveSessionModelRef` query path changed for the no-override + agentId case (skips stale runtime values in the persisted-model fallback), but all observable behavior is preserved or improved.

---

target.title: fix(msteams): bound SSO API JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

- Routes the live Microsoft Teams `signin.token-exchange` and `signin.verify-state` routes through OpenClaw's bounded SSO User Token helper instead of the Teams SDK's unbounded axios `res.data` path.
- Keeps the existing sender-policy gate and preserves token persistence for both `activity.from.id` and `activity.from.aadObjectId` aliases.
- Preserves the SDK cloud-specific Bot Framework User Token service URL, so USGov/USGovDoD/China SSO routes keep using the same token host as the SDK route they replace.
- Keeps the 16 MiB successful-response cap and existing non-OK error handling for Bot Framework User Token service calls.
- Adds production-route tests proving normal, oversized, and non-public-cloud User Token responses through the registered sign-in routes.

## Linked context

No linked issue; this is a narrow follow-up to the bounded-response-read hardening series for Microsoft Teams SSO.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: The previous PR version bounded only the direct SSO helper path. The production monitor-registered `signin.token-exchange` and `signin.verify-state` routes still delegated to the Teams SDK handlers, whose User Token client reads axios `res.data` without a response-size cap. This update moves those live routes onto OpenClaw's bounded helper while preserving the SDK cloud token-service URL via `app.cloud.tokenServiceUrl`.

Real environment tested: Linux x86-64, Node 22.22.0, local OpenClaw worktree with installed repo dependencies, real Node/Web `Response` streams, and the msteams extension test runtime.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/sdk.test.ts -- --run
./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/msteams/src/monitor.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/sdk.ts extensions/msteams/src/sso.ts extensions/msteams/src/sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/sdk.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/msteams/src/monitor.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/sdk.ts extensions/msteams/src/sso.ts extensions/msteams/src/sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/sdk.test.ts
```

Evidence after fix:
```text
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests  41 passed (41)
```
The new monitor lifecycle coverage calls the actual registered `signin.token-exchange` and `signin.verify-state` route callbacks. The success case verifies both routes call `fetch` through the bounded OpenClaw helper, persist both Teams user-id aliases, and do not call `app.onTokenExchange` / `app.onVerifyState`. The oversized case streams >16 MiB responses through those same registered routes and verifies they fail closed without saving a token or delegating to the SDK handlers. The USGov case verifies those same registered routes call `https://tokengcch.botframework.azure.us/api/usertoken/...`, proving the bounded replacement preserves SDK cloud token routing instead of falling back to the public Bot Framework token host.

Observed result after fix: Oversized successful Bot Framework User Token responses are capped before JSON parsing on the live SSO route path. Normal token exchange and verify-state responses still return `{ status: 200 }` and persist tokens for later OpenClaw use. Non-public Teams cloud SSO keeps the SDK's configured User Token service host.

What was not tested: A live Microsoft Teams tenant / Bot Framework OAuth connection. No tenant credentials are available in this environment.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/sdk.test.ts -- --run` - 4 files, 41 tests passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check ...` - all matched files use the correct format.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ...` - passed.

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Only for oversized successful Bot Framework User Token responses: they now fail closed at 16 MiB instead of being read unbounded.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No.
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? Yes, intentionally narrows the live SSO network read boundary; endpoint paths, auth headers, cloud token hosts, and token persistence semantics are preserved.
- What is the highest-risk area? Compatibility of replacing the SDK sign-in route delegate with the local bounded implementation.
- How is that risk mitigated? Tests exercise the registered production route callbacks for token-exchange and verify-state success, oversized-response failure, and USGov cloud token-host preservation; dependency inspection shows the SDK handlers perform the same User Token calls through unbounded axios `res.data`.

## Current review state

- Next action: ClawSweeper re-review for the previous cloud token-service URL blocker.
- Waiting on: CI for commit `b770b4b30122caed9624b6366d4ad8880dc6dc04`.

target.title: fix(cron): keep isolated run status ok when delivery fails
target.body:
## Summary

Scheduled isolated `agentTurn` cron jobs could finish a successful isolated session yet have the outer scheduled run persisted with `status=error` when the post-run delivery phase failed. This patch keeps execution `status=ok` and records the delivery failure separately, so cron run logs report `status=ok` with `deliveryStatus=not-delivered` instead of a false execution failure.

## Root cause

In `finalizeCronRun` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts`), when the agent payload was non-fatal (`!hasFatalErrorPayload`), the dispatch outcome was returned verbatim:

```ts
if (!hasFatalErrorPayload || deliveryResult.result.status !== "ok") {
  return resultWithDeliveryMeta; // carries deliveryResult.result.status === "error"
}
```

A `dispatchCronDelivery` result of `status: "error"` (unresolved target / outbound send failure) therefore collapsed into the isolated agent execution status. `applyJobResult` then set `lastRunStatus=error`, incremented `consecutiveErrors`, and could trigger backoff / failure alerts for a session that actually succeeded.

The storage layer already keeps `status` (`CronRunStatus`) and `deliveryStatus` (`CronDeliveryStatus`) as separate columns; the bug was purely that `run.ts` contaminated `status` before persistence.

## Changes

- `finalizeCronRun`: when the agent payload is non-fatal and the run was not aborted, a delivery dispatch `status: "error"` now routes through `resolveRunOutcome` so execution `status` stays `ok`. Delivery failure is recorded via `delivered`/`deliveryAttempted` and delivery diagnostics, which drive the decoupled run-log `deliveryStatus` (`not-delivered`). Aborted runs and fatal agent payloads keep their `error` status.
- `resolveRunOutcome`: carries optional `deliveryDiagnostics` so the delivery error remains operator-visible in run diagnostics even when `status=ok`.
- Adds a regression test asserting a successful final report followed by a delivery dispatcher failure keeps `status=ok` with delivery failure metadata.

Scope is limited to cron finalization; no provider/channel code is touched.

## Decoupling rationale (status vs deliveryStatus)

`status` answers "did the isolated agent turn execute successfully" and `deliveryStatus` answers "did the result reach its destination". These are orthogonal: a turn can succeed and the announce/direct send can still fail. Collapsing them made every transient delivery error look like an agent failure and drove backoff/alerting. Keeping them decoupled means a delivery failure is surfaced (`deliveryStatus=not-delivered`, delivery diagnostics) without falsely failing the execution — avoiding any cross-cutting product-decision change to the scheduler's error semantics.

## Semantic change — for maintainer review

This PR changes one observable behavior — the run-log `status` for the "execution succeeded, delivery failed" path — so I want to lay out the semantics and blast radius explicitly rather than asking you to infer them. This is the only judgement call in the change; the code is otherwise a verbatim re-route.

**1. Why `status` / `deliveryStatus` decoupling is the correct semantics.** An isolated `agentTurn` is a self-contained unit of work: it either executes successfully and produces a final assistant report, or it does not. Post-run *delivery* (announce / direct send) is a separate, downstream phase that depends on transient externals (channel resolution, outbound network, provider availability). Today a successful, completed isolated session is retroactively re-labelled `status=error` purely because the announce send failed afterwards — i.e. work that finished is recorded as failed work. The storage layer already models these as two independent columns (`CronRunStatus` + `CronDeliveryStatus`); this PR just stops `run.ts` from contaminating the first with the second. The user who filed #94058 reached the same conclusion independently — their stated expected behavior is exactly "preserve the successful agent execution outcome and separately record the delivery failure phase."

**2. Blast radius on backoff / failure-alert is deliberately narrow.** Only one path changes: agent payload non-fatal (`!hasFatalErrorPayload`) **and** `deliveryResult.result.status === "error"` **and** the run was not aborted (`!params.isAborted()`). That path goes from `status=error` to `status=ok` + `deliveryStatus=not-delivered`. Everything else is untouched:

   - A genuine execution failure (`hasFatalErrorPayload`) still records `status=error` → `consecutiveErrors++` → backoff / failure alerts fire exactly as before.
   - An aborted run still records `status=error`.
   - A successful delivery still records `status=ok` + delivered.

   So real execution failures continue to drive backoff and alerting; only the false positives (succeeded-but-undelivered) stop doing so. The delivery failure is **not** swallowed — it remains operator-visible via `delivered=false`, `deliveryAttempted`, the `deliveryStatus=not-delivered` column, and the merged delivery diagnostics.

**3. Compatibility note (the `merge-risk: compatibility` label).** The risk to weigh is operators/tooling that currently key off `status=error` to detect *undelivered* runs. After this change those runs surface as `status=ok` + `deliveryStatus=not-delivered`, so any such consumer should read `deliveryStatus` (the column already exists for this purpose) rather than overloading `status`. There is no schema/migration change and no provider/channel code touched. I have kept the code change to the minimum re-route and surfaced the trade-off here so the call on the error-semantics is yours to make — happy to adjust framing or gate the behavior if you'd prefer a more conservative landing.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** A successful isolated `agentTurn` whose post-run delivery fails was persisted to the cron run log with `status=error`, making a successful session look like a failed run (and feeding error backoff/alerting).
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Linux at `upstream/main` head `7217477553f64701d2ba36e344ca1cd6be8ba54f`, dependencies hydrated, commands run from the repo root.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Drove the REAL `CronService` finalization (`applyJobResult` + `resolveDeliveryState`) for a successful isolated turn with a failing post-run delivery, persisted the resulting `finished` run record through the REAL `appendCronRunLog` into a REAL on-disk SQLite database (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), then READ IT BACK across the SQLite disk boundary via the REAL `readCronRunLogEntriesSync`. The injected finalization outcome is exactly what patched `run.ts` returns, validated independently by the new vitest regression test.
- **Evidence after fix:** SQLite disk readback (console-intercept disabled):

  ```text
  [PROOF after-fix] finished event: {"jobId":"16ede2af-...","status":"ok","delivered":false,"deliveryStatus":"not-delivered"}
  [PROOF after-fix] SQLite readback: {"status":"ok","deliveryStatus":"not-delivered","delivered":false}
  ```

- **Negative control (pre-fix behavior reproduced):** Reverting only `run.ts` and re-running the regression test reproduces the bug (real `run.ts` output), and the same SQLite readback flow persists the collapsed status:

  ```text
  AssertionError: expected 'error' to be 'ok' // Object.is equality   (run.ts regression test, fix reverted)

  [PROOF pre-fix] SQLite readback: {"status":"error","deliveryStatus":"not-delivered","delivered":false,"deliveryError":"Message failed"}
  ```

- **Validation commands (all green after fix):**
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/isolated-agent/run.message-tool-policy.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.meta-error-status.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.double-announce.test.ts src/cron/service.persists-delivered-status.test.ts src/cron/service.runs-one-shot-main-job-disables-it.test.ts` -> 166 passed
  - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental false` -> exit 0
  - `oxfmt --check` on changed files -> all formatted
  - `oxlint` on changed files -> exit 0

**Label**: proof: live SQLite run-log readback across disk (status=ok / deliveryStatus=not-delivered) + negative control reproducing the pre-fix collapsed status=error.

AI-assisted.

Fixes #94058

## Summary

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers for interactive `az login --use-device-code`
- align the stream-error path with the established `src/node-host/invoke.ts` lifecycle pattern: record the first stream error, send one SIGTERM, escalate to SIGKILL after a grace period, and settle from the child `close` event (with a bounded fallback for shells that never emit `close`)
- keep duplicate stream errors and late child `error` events idempotent: the first stream error wins and teardown runs once
- cover the lifecycle with mocked-timer regressions plus a real spawned local `az` substitute process over real stdio pipes
- collision check: no open PR found for the Microsoft Foundry az login stream-error issue or `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts`

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 3 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` — passed; 1 file, 2 tests passed (real local child-process proof)
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.test.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts` — passed

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Microsoft Foundry `az login --use-device-code` stdout/stderr stream errors are contained without an unhandled stream error, duplicate teardown, or settlement before the child closes.
Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout; the proof uses a PATH-injected local `az` substitute executable — a real spawned process with real stdio pipes, not the Azure CLI and not an in-process mocked child.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending Nextcloud Talk messages or reactions could have the send workflow wait indefinitely when the Talk server accepts the HTTP connection but never responds.

## Why This Change Was Made

Nextcloud Talk's preflight path already passes a request timeout into `fetchWithSsrFGuard`; this change applies the same bounded request behavior to message and reaction sends while preserving the existing SSRF policy, headers, and response handling.

## User Impact

Operators get a bounded failure instead of a stuck outbound send when a self-hosted or remote Talk endpoint hangs after accepting the connection.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(tool-payload): enforce UTF-8 byte limits for serialized payloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where plain-text tool-call repair could accept serialized JSON or XML-style payloads whose UTF-8 size exceeded `maxPayloadBytes` when their text contained multibyte characters. Both parser paths previously relied on UTF-16 code-unit counts at the acceptance boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The parser now applies one UTF-8 byte-length helper to both formats. JSON validates the complete serialized object after its structural scan. XML parameters report each disjoint serialized segment's byte length, allowing cumulative enforcement without repeatedly encoding the entire growing prefix.

This preserves the existing parser grammar and public option while making the documented byte limit accurate for every accepted serialization.

## User Impact

Tool-call repair consistently rejects oversized serialized tool arguments for ASCII and multibyte text, preventing over-limit payloads from being promoted into executable tool calls.

target.title: feat(exec): deny-over-allow exec approval denylist (#6615)
target.body:
Fixes #6615. Supersedes #92456 (author inactive since 2026-06-12, no response to review, conflicts with main — full credit to @Hidetsugu55 for the STOP-list concept and dual-host enforcement approach, both kept here).

## Update — re-review 2 (clawsweeper P1 blockers resolved)

The previous review's three P1 blockers were "contract declared but not wired." All three are now wired end-to-end, with focused tests on each exact path plus refreshed real-behavior proof. Also merged latest `origin/main` (resolves the CONFLICTING/behind-main note).

- **[P1] Wire `tools.exec.denylist` into config schema + gateway caller** — `denylist` added to the strict zod `ToolExecBaseShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`, non-empty-pattern refinement) so `openclaw config validate` accepts it and rejects malformed entries; threaded as `execConfigDenylist` through `agent-tools.ts` → `bash-tools.exec.ts` → `processGatewayAllowlist`, unioned across global + per-agent layers (`resolveEffectiveExecDenylist`). Tests: `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`.
- **[P1] Pass denylist hits into node-host `system.run`** — `invoke-system-run.ts` now evaluates the effective denylist (openclaw.json global + per-agent + `exec-approvals.json` file layer) and passes `denylisted`/`denylistReason` into `evaluateSystemRunPolicy`; the model auto-reviewer is hard-blocked on a hit (human-only), and unanalyzable commands fail closed. Tests: `invoke-system-run.test.ts` (+ node denial reason `denylist-hit`).
- **[P1] Add denylist to exec-approval protocol writes** — `ExecApprovalsDenylistEntrySchema` + `denylist` added to `ExecApprovalsPolicyFields` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts` so `exec.approvals.set` / `exec.approvals.node.set` round-trip the field. Tests: `exec-approvals-validators.test.ts`.

Two extra hardening changes made while wiring the above:

- **Real defect fix:** `sanitizeExecApprovalPolicy` (`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`) was silently dropping the defaults-layer `denylist` on every `saveExecApprovals` write — a routine policy write would disarm an operator's STOP list. Now normalized and preserved.
- **Standalone gate:** the gateway host now has an independent `requiresDenylistApproval || …` short-circuit in `processGatewayAllowlist`, so the deny-over-allow guarantee cannot regress even if `requiresExecApproval`'s denylist handling ever changes.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's exec approvals support allowlists but no denylist: there is no way to force human approval (or denial) for specific dangerous commands when an agent runs at `security=full` / `ask=off`, or when a broad allowlist/durable trust would otherwise auto-approve them. #6615 asks for a deny-over-allow screening layer so commands like `git push --force` or `rm -rf` patterns always require an explicit human decision, regardless of permissive settings.

## Fix

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.ts`: entry normalization, strict validation (`collectExecDenylistErrors`), and `resolveEffectiveExecDenylist` (de-duplicated union across layers — deny anywhere = deny).
- **Both config layers**: `openclaw.json` `tools.exec.denylist` (global + per-agent) **and** `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` (defaults + `*` + agent), wired through both exec hosts (see Update above).
- **Shared pattern language**: denylist patterns reuse the existing allowlist glob compiler via a new `matchesExecGlob` export — no second matcher to keep in sync (`*` → `[^/]*`, `**` → `.*`, `?` → `[^/]`).
- **Deny wins first**: a hit forces approval ahead of `ask=off`, `security=full`, allowlist hits, and durable allow-always trust, on both the gateway exec host and node-host `system.run` (node denial reason `denylist-hit`). Explicit allow-once approval still clears a hit; `security=deny` still wins overall.
- Conservative fallback: unanalyzable command + configured denylist ⇒ approval required, not fail-open. Basename variants and `bash -c "..."` inner payloads are screened.

## Evidence

**Typecheck (repo's real TS-Go checker):** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both clean on this branch. (Stock `tsc` throws a bogus TS4058 in `src/secrets/config-io.ts` that tsgo does not — pre-existing on `main`.)

**Focused tests — all green on the exact paths flagged:**
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts` — 19 (normalize/dedupe, both-layer union, exact/glob/basename/wrapper matches, conservative fallback, precedence).
- `src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts` — 19 and `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — 36 (node-host `system.run` enforcement, config-layer union, human-only, `denylist-hit`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 54 (gateway standalone denylist gate at `security=full`/`ask=off`).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts` — 8 (protocol/file denylist round-trip).
- `src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` — 39 and `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 23 (config schema accept/validate + label/help coverage).

> Note: on a host that symlinks `head` to cargo-coreutils, one unrelated pre-existing test (`processGatewayAllowlist > uses a plan-backed enforced command…`) fails on a `/usr/bin/head` vs `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/head` path assertion. It is environmental and independent of this PR (our diff to that test file is additive only).

**Real behavior proof** (real decision code path via `node --import tsx`, no test doubles — `git push --force origin main` allowlisted + durable-trusted at `security=full`/`ask=off`, denylist supplied through the openclaw.json config layer exactly as the wired callers do):

```
## BEFORE (control: no denylist configured)
[gateway-host] command="git push --force origin main" security=full ask=off allowlisted=true durable=true -> AUTO-RUN
[node-host]    command="git push --force origin main" -> ALLOWED

## AFTER (denylist configured via openclaw.json tools.exec.denylist)
denylist = [{"pattern":"git push*--force*","reason":"history rewrite"}]
[gateway-host] -> APPROVAL REQUIRED
[node-host]    -> DENIED (denylist-hit)

## AFTER + explicit allow-once approval
[node-host]    -> ALLOWED (approval cleared the hit)
```

## Scope notes

- Contract is now complete across config schema, gateway protocol write schema, gateway host caller, node-host `system.run`, docs/help (`schema.help.ts` + `schema.labels.ts`), tests, and real proof.
- No drive-by refactors.


## Node-host prompt parity (b0164f0fe8a, 2026-07-09)

Review found that the `host=node` `security=full`/`ask=off` fast path invoked `system.run` directly before prepare/approval registration, so a denylist STOP rule hard-denied server-side (`denylist-hit`) instead of raising the documented human allow-once prompt.

Fixed for prompt parity (recommended option):

- The direct fast path is taken only when the caller-visible effective denylist is **known empty**: the `openclaw.json` config layer is empty AND the node approvals-file denylist (fetched via `exec.approvals.node.get`) is known and empty. Fetch failures fail **closed** into the prepare path.
- On the prepare path, the effective denylist (config layer + node approvals-file layer) is evaluated caller-side; a hit forces a registered human approval request even at full/off, mirroring the gateway host: auto-review is excluded (human-only), and `allow-always` is downgraded to one-shot so no durable trust can be minted from a denylist hit.
- Non-matching commands with a configured denylist still auto-run (via the prepare path); setups with no denylist keep the direct fast path.

Focused tests added in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts`: config-layer hit registers an approval request (no direct denial), approvals-file hit registers an approval request, non-matching denylist auto-runs, known-empty denylist keeps the fast path, approvals fetch failure fails closed to prepare. `vitest run src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts --pool=forks` => 4 files, 146 tests passed; tsgo typecheck clean.

Honest proof status: production decision-function proof and the focused node-host approval-registration tests are in; a live gateway+node prompt -> allow-once -> runs-exactly-once capture is being prepared on a dedicated QA host and will be appended when complete.

Known residual (intentional, documented here): a denylist configured ONLY in the node machine's own local `openclaw.json` remains invisible to the gateway-side caller and still hard-denies server-side (fail-closed). The two operator surfaces this PR documents (`tools.exec.denylist` config layer and the exec-approvals file) now both get prompt parity on host=node.

target.title: fix(gateway): cap pricing cache entries to prevent unbounded memory growth (#101543)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101543. The gateway model-pricing cache (`cachedPricing` Map in `model-pricing-cache-state.ts`) has no upper bound. Long-running OpenClaw processes with many dynamic models or plugins accumulate pricing entries on every 24h refresh cycle without eviction, eventually causing OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES = 1000` and caps the Map in `replaceGatewayModelPricingCache` using **access-aware (LRU) eviction**:

1. Merges existing cache entries (carrying access history) with new refresh data
2. Sorts by last-access timestamp descending (newest first), then by key for determinism
3. Keeps the top `MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES` entries
4. **Prunes `pricingAccessTimestamps` after every replacement** so the side-map metadata cannot outlive evicted cache entries

Access timestamps are recorded in `getCachedGatewayModelPricing` on every cache hit, so models actively queried by running sessions survive refresh cycles.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — access-aware eviction + metadata pruning

```
1. Active entry seeded and accessed: ✓ found
2. Refresh payload: 1100 entries (over limit by 100)
3. Cache capped at: 1000 (limit: 1000)
   ✓ size === MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES
4. Access-aware retention:
   zzz-active/zzz-model: retained (input=100)
   ✓ recently-accessed entry preserved
```

Run with: `node --import tsx/esm src/gateway/proof-pricing-cache-eviction.ts`

### Vitest

```
pnpm test src/gateway/model-pricing-cache.test.ts
  [...] "caps cache entries at MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES and preserves recently-accessed entries" — passed
```

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/gateway/model-pricing-cache-state.ts` | +`MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES`; +`pricingAccessTimestamps` access tracking; +merge-sort-evict in `replaceGatewayModelPricingCache`; +`prunePricingAccessTimestamps` metadata cleanup |
| `src/gateway/model-pricing-cache.test.ts` | Enhanced test: active entry retention + tail entry eviction |

## Changelog

- **v2** (6fc3d8b): First-N truncation `Array.from(nextPricing).slice(0, 1000)`
- **v3** (53bb644): Access-aware LRU eviction — merge existing + new, sort by recency
- **v4** (aafb24a): Prune `pricingAccessTimestamps` to retained `cachedPricing` keys after every replacement, preventing unbounded metadata growth

target.title: fix(google): add timeout to Vertex ADC token refresh
target.body:
Related: #95865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Google Vertex `authorized_user` Application Default Credentials token refresh can wait indefinitely when the OAuth token endpoint accepts the request but never sends a response.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vertex ADC token refresh already bounds the token response body after a response arrives, but the fetch itself had no deadline. This change adds a 30s token-refresh request timeout while preserving the existing ADC credential lookup, token cache, token-expiry handling, and bounded response-body parsing.

## User Impact

Operators using Google Vertex with local `authorized_user` ADC get a bounded authentication failure instead of a stuck provider request when the Google OAuth token refresh HTTP request stalls after connection acceptance.

## Collision / Differentiation Check

Open PRs touch the same Vertex ADC file, so this PR is intentionally narrow and differentiated:

- #98507 bounds token response body reads to prevent OOM after a response arrives; this PR bounds the request before any response arrives.
- #101035 supports `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID`; this PR does not alter project/env resolution.
- #91222 handles transient pre-stream failures and stale ADC retry behavior; this PR does not add retry behavior.

target.title: Gateway: allow extension origins in browser allowlist
target.body: ## Summary Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets: - Problem: `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` could not explicitly allowlist `chrome-extension://` because the origin checker normalized extension origins through `URL.origin`, which becomes `"null"` for that scheme. - Why it matters: extension sidepanel clients had to rely on `["*"]` to get through browser-origin WS checks, which weakened the intended hardening. - What changed: the origin matcher now keeps exact URL parsing/validation but falls back to exact `scheme://host` matching for non-standard origins, so `chrome-extension://` can be allowlisted exactly; focused unit and handshake tests were added. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): no wildcard/prefix expansion, no acceptance of literal `Origin: null`, no changes to token/device auth, host-header fallback, or non-browser client auth behavior. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs - [x] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [x] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #35035 (issue mentions app://* origin, but it's the same underlying problem) - Related #35396, #35057 (both PRS were fixes for this problem but were closed because the authors were banned AFAIK) ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` can now contain exact extension origins such as `chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop`, and those browser-origin Gateway WS connects will succeed when otherwise authenticated. - Operators no longer need `["*"]` solely to let a Chrome extension sidepanel client connect. - Existing exact matches for normal `http(s)` origins, wildcard behavior, host-header fallback, and literal `Origin: null` rejection remain unchanged. ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? target.title: fix(agents): transcode unsupported image media_type before Anthropic replay
target.body:
Closes #102323

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on a Claude/Anthropic model with no media-understanding provider (so inbound images are forwarded as image blocks, not transcribed) would get **no reply at all** when they sent an iPhone HEIC photo — or any `image/heic`, `image/tiff`, or `image/bmp` image — that was already within OpenClaw's size and dimension limits.

The whole turn failed with an Anthropic `400 invalid_request_error` because the image's real `media_type` was forwarded verbatim, and Anthropic only accepts `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/gif`, or `image/webp`. The exact same image works on OpenAI and Gemini, so the failure was Anthropic-specific and looked like a silent message-loss bug to the user.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared image sanitizer (`src/agents/tool-images.ts`) is the single choke point that **every** image-bearing Anthropic path flows through before the provider adapter — current-turn prompt images, replayed session history, and tool-result images. The Anthropic adapters (`packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` and `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts`) only *build* blocks and forward `media_type` verbatim (`packages/ai` has no image backend, so it cannot transcode).

Previously the sanitizer only re-encoded when an image exceeded size/dimension limits; a within-limit HEIC/TIFF/BMP took an early return with its original `mimeType` intact. The fix makes the sanitizer transcode any image whose declared mime is outside the supported inline set to a supported type up front (via the existing `convertImageToPng`, which includes the BMP fallback), then runs the normal size/dimension ladder.

Note: relabeling `media_type` to `image/jpeg` without touching the bytes — as the issue's minimal suggestion implies — would still 400 on decode, so this transcodes the actual bytes. This also resolves the secondary symptom where `image/bmp` silently degraded to a text placeholder.

## User Impact

Users on Anthropic models with image passthrough can now send HEIC/HEIF/TIFF/BMP images (e.g. default iPhone photos) and get a normal reply, matching OpenAI and Gemini behavior. No config change or migration required.

## Evidence

### Full runtime proof — 18 tests across 3 files (`main` @ 03aca2c)

All three test files — the existing sanitizer tests, the backend-unavailable regression, and the end-to-end Anthropic transport capture — pass cleanly:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/agents/tool-images.test.ts \
    src/agents/tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts \
    src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.image-mediatype.test.ts \
    --reporter=verbose

target.title: fix(cron): suppress same-target failure notice after partial announce delivery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A cron `--announce` job whose report actually reached the channel could still post a `Cron job "<name>" failed: <error>` notice to that same channel when the durable send reported `partial_failed` (visible content sent before the error). Recipients saw a successful report immediately followed by a false failure alarm.

This addresses the source-backed half of #102367 (false failure reporting + same-target failure re-announce). The intermittent duplicate `chat.postMessage` trigger reported there remains open and is intentionally out of scope for this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

`deliverCronAnnouncePayload` threw on `partial_failed` exactly like a full failure (`src/cron/delivery.ts`), so the command-cron catch flipped the run to `error` and the gateway failure fallback (`src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts`) could not distinguish "nothing was delivered" from "delivered, then errored" — and re-announced the failure to the very target that had just received the report.

Fix shape:

- `sendCronAnnouncePayloadStrict` now returns a closed outcome: `{ status: "sent" } | { status: "partial_failed"; error }`, throwing only when nothing reached the target. The throw-on-partial behavior dates to the 2026-05-09 delivery API consolidation (a4b17d65a8), not a product decision.
- The command-cron path keeps marking the run as `error` on partial delivery (strict non-best-effort announce semantics are preserved) but records `sentBeforeError: true` on the existing `CronDeliveryTrace`, which already rides the finished cron event.
- The failure-notification dispatcher skips only the primary-target fallback notice when `sentBeforeError` is set. Explicit `failureDestination` routes and webhooks still fire.
- `resolveDeliveryState` records the failure notification as `not-requested` (instead of `not-delivered`) for this case so job state matches the suppression.
- Sibling surface: the isolated-agent delivery path already tracked `partialDeliverySucceededBeforeFailure` internally; it now surfaces the same `sentBeforeError` fact through `DispatchCronDeliveryState` into its delivery trace, so isolated announce jobs get the same suppression.

## User Impact

No more false `Cron job "<name>" failed` posts into a channel that just received the announce output. Runs with genuinely partial delivery still surface as errors in cron state, run logs, failure-alert backoff, and non-primary failure destinations. The `--best-effort-deliver` workaround from the issue is no longer needed for this symptom.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/cron src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts src/gateway/server.cron.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron-lazy.test.ts` — 128 files / 1370 tests green.
- `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `check:changed` lanes green (run locally on macOS; Testbox/Crabbox delegation was unavailable on this machine — no `crabbox` binary installed).
- New regression tests:
  - `src/cron/delivery.failure-notify.test.ts`: strict send outcome contract (sent / partial returns / full failure throws) and partial failure-notice logging.
  - `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts`: primary-target notice suppressed on `sentBeforeError`, still sent when nothing delivered, explicit failure destinations unaffected.
  - `src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts`: end-to-end command cron — partial announce → run `error` with no failure re-announce; full announce failure → fallback notice to the primary target preserved.

target.title: fix(crestodian): run approval-intent classifier on the utilityModel, not flagship (#102360)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Crestodian approval-intent classifier (`classifyCrestodianApprovalIntent`, `src/crestodian/approval-intent.ts`) resolves the completion model **without** `useUtilityModel: true`, so an ambiguous approval reply that reaches the model path runs on the agent's **flagship** model to decide a single approve/decline/other label. It was the only member of the simple-completion family (e.g. `conversation-label-generator.ts`) that omitted the flag, so every ambiguous approval reply is billed at flagship pricing for a fixed ~8-token structured answer. Fixes #102360.

## Why This Change Was Made

A one-word bounded classification is exactly the "utility work" the rest of the family already runs on the configured `utilityModel`. `prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` already supports `useUtilityModel` (resolves `agents.defaults.utilityModel`); the classifier just wasn't passing it. Adding `useUtilityModel: true` aligns it with the family and the cheaper tier.

## User Impact

Operators who configure a distinct `utilityModel` (the intended cheap tier for bounded classification) stop paying flagship pricing for ambiguous approval-flow replies. No behavior change to the classification result — only the model tier that judges it.

## Evidence

Real `classifyCrestodianApprovalIntent` call with an ambiguous message (model path), capturing what model prep receives:
```
before (main):    prepare called with useUtilityModel = undefined   ← flagship
after  (this PR): prepare called with useUtilityModel = true        ← utilityModel
```
Added a regression test asserting `prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` is called with `{ useUtilityModel: true }`. `tsgo:core` 0 errors; `approval-intent.test.ts` green (8 tests: 7 existing + 1 new).

target.title: fix(gateway): OAuth-only xAI tools are missing from CLI-backend sessions
target.body:
Closes #101967

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running CLI-backend sessions (e.g., `claude-cli`) with OAuth-only xAI auth would never see the `x_search` and `code_execution` tools on the session tool surface. Because subagents inherit the parent session's tool list, the tools were also stripped from native-runtime Grok subagents spawned from a claude-cli main session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway loopback MCP bridge that feeds CLI-backend sessions resolved plugin tools without passing an `authProfileStore`. Native embedded runs already passed the store, which let the xAI plugin register search/code-execution tools when an OAuth profile was present. This change threads the auth profile store through the same path and ensures the loopback surface uses the agent-local store without silently falling back to main credentials:

- `resolveGatewayScopedTools` now accepts and forwards `authProfileStore` and `agentDir` to `createOpenClawTools`.
- `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` / `McpLoopbackToolCache` accept `authProfileStore` and `agentDir`; the cache key includes `agentDir` so different agents do not share tool entries.
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` forwards its already-loaded `authStore` and resolved `agentDir` when computing prompt tools.
- The MCP loopback HTTP server resolves the per-session agent directory, loads the agent-local auth profile store, and passes both into tool resolution.
- `loadAuthProfileStoreForSecretsRuntime` gains an `excludeMainOverlay` option; the loopback path uses it so an expired or missing agent-local OAuth profile does not silently inherit the main store's OAuth identity.

## User Impact

CLI-backend sessions with OAuth-only xAI auth now correctly surface `x_search` and `code_execution`, and subagents spawned from those sessions inherit the tools as expected. Agent-local OAuth credentials stay scoped to the agent on the loopback surface.

## Evidence

- New focused tests:
  - `src/gateway/tool-resolution.auth.test.ts` verifies `resolveGatewayScopedTools` forwards `authProfileStore` and `agentDir` to `createOpenClawTools` on both loopback and HTTP surfaces.
  - `src/gateway/mcp-http.runtime.auth.test.ts` verifies `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` forwards `authProfileStore` and `agentDir` to `resolveGatewayScopedTools`.
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` verifies `prepareCliRunContext` passes the loaded auth store and `agentDir` to loopback tool resolution.
  - `src/agents/auth-profiles/profiles.test.ts` verifies `loadAuthProfileStoreForSecretsRuntime(agentDir, { excludeMainOverlay: true })` does not inherit main OAuth profiles.
  - `extensions/xai/src/xai-oauth-tool-registration.test.ts` verifies the xAI plugin registers `x_search` and `code_execution` when an OAuth auth context is present.

- Existing suites still pass:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts src/gateway/tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/tools-invoke-http.cron-regression.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/auth-profiles/profiles.test.ts`

## Real behavior proof

The following is a redacted runtime transcript produced by `scripts/proof/xai-oauth-loopback-tools.ts`. It exercises the actual changed gateway path:

1. Builds a real plugin registry and registers the bundled xAI plugin through a real `registerTool` handler (so `code_execution` and `x_search` are actually recorded in the registry).
2. Loads an OAuth-only xAI auth profile store (tokens redacted).
3. Calls `resolveGatewayScopedTools({ surface: "loopback", authProfileStore, agentDir })` — the same function used by the CLI-backend loopback/MCP tool surface.
4. Prints the resulting MCP `tools/list` JSON-RPC response.

All private tokens, account IDs, phone numbers, IPs, and non-public endpoints are redacted.

```bash
node --import tsx scripts/proof/xai-oauth-loopback-tools.ts
```

```text
[xai-oauth-loopback-proof] registered plugin tool count: 2
[xai-oauth-loopback-proof] registered plugin tool names: code_execution, x_search
[agents/tool-policy] tool policy removed 5 tool(s) via tools.profile (coding): agents_list, gateway, message, nodes, tts
[xai-oauth-loopback-proof] resolved loopback tool names: code_execution, create_goal, cron, get_goal, image_generate, memory_get, memory_search, session_status, sessions_history, sessions_list, sessions_send, sessions_spawn, sessions_yield, skill_workshop, subagents, update_goal, update_plan, video_generate, web_fetch, web_search, x_search
[xai-oauth-loopback-proof] MCP tools/list response:
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "proof-tools-list",
  "result": {
    "tools": [
      ...
      {
        "name": "code_execution",
        "description": "Run sandboxed Python analysis with xAI. Use for calculations, tabulation, summaries, and chart-style analysis without local machine access."
      },
      ...
      {
        "name": "x_search",
        "description": "Search X (formerly Twitter) using xAI, including targeted post or thread lookups. For per-post stats like reposts, replies, bookmarks, or views, prefer the exact post URL or status ID."
      }
    ]
  }
}
PASS: x_search and code_execution are present on the loopback surface.
```

This confirms that after the fix, the OAuth-only xAI auth profile store and resolved agent directory flow through the changed gateway loopback path and both `x_search` and `code_execution` are surfaced.

target.title: fix(msteams): lowercase content type so attachment classification is case-insensitive
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`normalizeContentType` (`extensions/msteams/src/attachments/shared.ts`) only trimmed its input — it never lowercased. MIME types are **case-insensitive per RFC 2045**, and MS Teams relay payloads (SharePoint, OneDrive, Bot Framework CDN) routinely emit mixed-case values such as `"Image/PNG"` or `"Application/Vnd.Microsoft.Teams.File.Download.Info"`.

Every downstream comparison in the attachments module assumes a **lowercased** value:
- `isLikelyImageAttachment`: `contentType.startsWith("image/")` (shared.ts:241)
- `isDownloadableAttachment`: `contentType === "application/vnd.microsoft.teams.file.download.info"` (shared.ts:274)
- `isHtmlAttachment`: `contentType.startsWith("text/html")` (shared.ts:291)
- `html.ts`: `startsWith("text/html")`, `startsWith("application/vnd.microsoft.card.")` (lines 119-120, 177)
- `download.ts`: `contentType === "application/vnd.microsoft.teams.file.download.info"` (line 42)

So a mixed-case inbound attachment was **silently misclassified**: an image became a document, an HTML body was skipped, and a Teams file-download-info attachment was not resolved for download.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** `normalizeContentType` returned the trimmed-but-original-casing string, while all consumers compare against lowercase literals.
- **Fix:** Lowercase in `normalizeContentType` (`value.trim().toLowerCase()`). MIME types are case-insensitive by spec, so lowercasing can never turn a previously-matching value into a non-match — it only adds matches. One change fixes all six call sites at once.
- The sibling `inferPlaceholder` in the **same file** (shared.ts:228) already lowercases via `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty`; this aligns the two code paths. The canonical repo helper `normalizeMimeType` (`packages/media-core/src/mime.ts`) also lowercases.

## User Impact

Inbound MS Teams attachments with mixed-case `contentType` are now classified correctly: images are recognized as images (inline/display + download routing), HTML attachment bodies are extracted, and Teams file-download-info attachments resolve their download URL. Lowercase `contentType` values are unaffected. No behavior change for non-Teams code paths.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue).

## Evidence

Reproduced with a `node` runtime script importing `normalizeContentType`, `isLikelyImageAttachment`, and `isDownloadableAttachment` to verify mixed-case MIME handling.

Terminal output of `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-msteams-content-type.mjs` after the fix:

```
[PASS] normalizeContentType("Image/PNG") = "image/png"
[PASS] normalizeContentType("Application/Vnd.Microsoft.Teams.File.Download.Info") = "application/vnd.microsoft.teams.file.download.info"
[PASS] isLikelyImageAttachment("Image/PNG", no ext) = true (matches lowercase true)
[PASS] isDownloadableAttachment(mixed-case download.info) = true (matches lowercase true)
[PASS] application/pdf is not an image (regression)
[PASS] undefined input -> undefined
[PASS] whitespace-only -> undefined
```

Before the fix, an inbound attachment with `contentType: "Image/PNG"` and no filename-extension hint was misclassified as a non-image, and the mixed-case Teams download-info `===` check missed its branch. After the fix, mixed-case types classify identically to their lowercase forms; non-image types still rejected; undefined/whitespace still return `undefined`.

**Also fixed: message-handler HTML text path (follow-up to review finding).** `extractTextFromHtmlAttachments` (`extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts`) guarded its loop with an exact `attachment.contentType !== "text/html"` check — the same case-sensitivity gap. A mixed-case `TEXT/HTML` attachment (body text only) was skipped, so the message entered the agent path with empty `htmlText`. The guard now routes through `normalizeContentType`, and the function is exported with regression coverage.

Terminal output of `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-msteams-html.mjs` (guard reaches HTML body extraction? true = body extracted, false = skipped → empty message):

```
[PASS] mixed-case upper ("TEXT/HTML"): old=false fixed=true
[PASS] mixed-case title ("Text/Html"): old=false fixed=true
[PASS] whitespace-padded ("  text/html  "): old=false fixed=true
[PASS] lowercase (regression) ("text/html"): old=true fixed=true
[PASS] non-HTML (regression) ("application/vnd.microsoft.card.hero"): old=false fixed=false
[PASS] undefined (undefined): old=false fixed=false

Message impact: TEXT/HTML attachment with body text
  OLD: htmlText = "" (exact guard skipped it)
  FIX: htmlText = "Hello Teams"
[PASS] fixed path extracts body text that old path dropped
```

The old exact guard skipped a `TEXT/HTML` attachment (empty `htmlText`); the fixed normalized guard extracts its body text. Non-HTML and undefined attachments are still skipped.

## Real behavior proof

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | `normalizeContentType` did not lowercase, so `isLikelyImageAttachment({ contentType: "Image/PNG", name: "download" })` returned `false` (no filename-extension rescue) and the Teams download-info `===` check missed mixed-case types. |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22, commit `caede8a4a91d2ce3c72bdd837cb8af0e5f5aceb0` |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-msteams-content-type.mjs` — imports `normalizeContentType`, `isLikelyImageAttachment`, `isDownloadableAttachment` and checks mixed-case image/download-info recognition plus ASCII/undefined/whitespace regressions. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output):
```

[PASS] normalizeContentType("Application/Vnd.Microsoft.Teams.File.Download.Info") = "application/vnd.microsoft.teams.file.download.info"
[PASS] isLikelyImageAttachment("Image/PNG", no ext) = true (matches lowercase true)
[PASS] isDownloadableAttachment(mixed-case download.info) = true (matches lowercase true)
[PASS] application/pdf is not an image (regression)
[PASS] undefined input -> undefined
[PASS] whitespace-only -> undefined
``` |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | Mixed-case `contentType` values are lowercased, so image/HTML/download-info attachments are now classified identically to their lowercase forms. Non-image types still rejected; undefined/empty/whitespace still return `undefined`. |
| 6 | What was not tested | Live Teams tenant traffic with a real mixed-case relay payload (no credentialled tenant here); the colocated unit tests cover `normalizeContentType`, `isLikelyImageAttachment`, and `isDownloadableAttachment` directly across mixed-case/lowercase/regression cases. |

## What Problem This Solves

Codex app inventory refresh diagnostics could serialize a long top-level error message with a dangling UTF-16 surrogate when an `app/list` failure crossed the 500-code-unit limit. Nested error-data strings already used safe truncation, but the top-level message did not.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Route both top-level messages and nested error-data strings through one `truncateSerializedErrorText` owner.
- Reuse the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` primitive and preserve the existing 500-unit limit, ellipsis, HTML omission, secret redaction, cache behavior, and protocol.
- Add an exact regression where an emoji straddles the top-level message boundary.

The upstream Codex contract was checked directly: `app/list` is registered as an unserialized request in `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs:732-735`; its response is `AppsListResponse` in `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/apps.rs:159-168`; and concurrent connector failures become JSON-RPC internal-error strings in `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/apps_processor.rs:164-279`. OpenClaw therefore owns sanitizing those error strings before retaining and logging diagnostics.

## User Impact

Codex app inventory refresh diagnostics remain valid UTF-16 when long upstream errors contain emoji or other astral characters at the truncation boundary. Normal errors and app inventory behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

Exact head: `87ea557c48f0611b7047f85b1359cbd5802be513`

target.title: fix(codex): fail-closed on unknown item statuses and warn on dropped notifications
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Codex event projector **failed open** on protocol drift: unrecognized item statuses were mapped to `"completed"` (so a tool that actually failed or carried an unknown status was projected as **success**), and unknown notification methods plus thread/turn correlation mismatches were **silently dropped** with no breadcrumb — converting future Codex protocol drift into wrong results instead of diagnosable errors.

Closes #99269.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three fail-open / silent-drop sites in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts`:

1. **`itemStatus` fail-open** — the trailing fallthrough returned `"completed"` for every unrecognized status. Now fail-closes to `"failed"` (mirroring the file's own `auditNativeToolTerminalStatus`, which already refuses to assume success for ambiguous statuses). Known mappings (`failed`/`error`→failed, `declined`→blocked, `inProgress`/`in_progress`/`running`→running, `completed`/missing→completed) are **unchanged**.
2. **Unknown notification method** — the `handleNotification` `default:` case dropped unknown methods silently. Now warns once per method (behavior unchanged — still dropped).
3. **Thread/turn correlation mismatch** — the early `return;`s dropped mismatched notifications silently. Now warns once per `method+thread+turn` (behavior unchanged). `turn/completed` is guarded: a `turn/completed` for a non-active turn is dropped by the turn-router before reaching the projector, so a correlation warning there would be unreachable.

Warn-once dedup uses `Set`s keyed per `item-type+status`, per `method`, and per `method+thread+turn` — rate-limited diagnostics at the projector boundary, as the issue asks. The item-status `Set` is module-level (process-lifetime rate-limiting for a bounded status set); the notification `Set`s are per-projector-instance.

## Codex protocol verification (hard gate)

Per the repo's Codex gate, I personally inspected `openai/codex` (`codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/`) for the item-status values Codex actually emits:

- `CommandExecutionStatus.ts` → `inProgress | completed | failed | declined`
- `PatchApplyStatus.ts` (fileChange) → `inProgress | completed | failed | declined`
- `McpToolCallStatus.ts`, `DynamicToolCallStatus.ts`, `CollabAgentToolCallStatus.ts` → `inProgress | completed | failed`
- `ImageGenerationItem.status` (free-form `String` in `ext/items/src/image_generation.rs`); the only emitter (`ext/image-generation/src/tool.rs`) sets `in_progress` / `failed` / `completed`.
- `TurnStatus.ts` → `completed | failed | inProgress | interrupted` — `interrupted` applies to **turns**, not items routed through `itemStatus`.

Every item-status literal Codex emits is already in the projector's known set, so the fail-closed path only catches genuinely-unknown/future strings. No status was added; `pausedByProtocol` / `queued` / `cancelled` / `needs_permission` / `unresolved` are **not** real Codex item statuses.

## User Impact

When Codex introduces a new item status (protocol drift), the projector no longer silently treats it as success — the tool result is marked `failed`/`isError` and a single rate-limited warning names the unrecognized status. Unknown notification methods and correlation mismatches now leave a breadcrumb instead of vanishing, making drift diagnosable. Behavior for all known statuses and for dropped notifications is otherwise unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused vitest (local, Node 24):
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` — **131 passed** (5→6 new tests added: unknown status→`failed`+`isError` + warn-once-per-status; a *second* unrecognized status (`queued`) still warns, confirming per-status dedup; unknown-method warn-once + drop preserved; correlation-mismatch warn-once + drop preserved; known statuses map correctly with zero warnings; `turn/completed` mismatch emits zero warnings).
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts -t "turn/completed"` — **2 passed | 115 skipped**, no regression. (4 unrelated `run-attempt` auth-profile/elicitation failures reproduce identically on `upstream/main` with this diff reverted — pre-existing, not caused by this change.)
- `tsgo` typecheck (`extensions/codex/tsconfig.json`): exit 0. `oxlint` on touched files: exit 0. `git diff --check`: clean.

Behavior preservation: warn calls are inserted strictly **before** the existing `return;`/`break;`/fallthrough (control flow unchanged); the test diff has **0 removed lines** (no existing assertion weakened); 125 pre-existing tests pass unmodified.

In-process real-behavior proof (vitest harness feeding `CodexAppServerEventProjector` directly — not a provider live-run):
```
scenario 1 — unknown status 'pausedByProtocol' (×2):
  item projected status = failed | isError = true ; unrecognized-status warnings = 1 (dedup)
scenario 2 — unknown method 'item/futureStatus/updated' (×2):
  unknown-method warnings = 1 (dedup) ; tool events emitted = 0 (dropped, unchanged)
scenario 3 — item/completed for turn 'turn-other' (active 'turn-1', ×2):
  correlation-mismatch warnings = 1 (dedup) ; tool events emitted = 0 (dropped, unchanged)
```

## Relation to existing PRs

- **#99754** takes the same correct fail-closed approach and is code-green, but is blocked on the contributor-proof gates this PR satisfies: it lacks the required `What Problem This Solves`/`Evidence` sections (the "Real behavior proof" gate) and a flaky QA Smoke e2e; it also does not guard `turn/completed` (a ClawSweeper noise flag).
- **#99287** has a fatal build defect (imports a never-defined `describeCodexNotificationCorrelation`) and a dirty merge.

This PR ships the evidence/proof sections, the `turn/completed` guard, regression tests (incl. per-status dedup), and a clean build.

target.title: fix(tool-payload): enforce UTF-8 byte limits for serialized payloads

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where plain-text tool-call repair could accept serialized JSON or XML-style payloads whose UTF-8 size exceeded `maxPayloadBytes` when their text contained multibyte characters. Both parser paths previously relied on UTF-16 code-unit counts at the acceptance boundary.

The parser now applies one UTF-8 byte-length helper to both formats. JSON validates the complete serialized object after its structural scan. XML parameters report each disjoint serialized segment's byte length, allowing cumulative enforcement without repeatedly encoding the entire growing prefix.

target.title: fix(feishu): preserve text before media attachments
target.body:
Closes #102390

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users would lose the assistant's visible text when a final reply contained both prose and a `MEDIA:` image attachment while streaming cards were active. The affected chat could show only the no-visible-reply fallback or an attachment without the intended explanation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Feishu reply dispatcher now closes the final streaming text card before sending regular media attachments, so the text is committed as visible content before the attachment path runs. If the streaming close accepts no text content, the dispatcher falls back to a normal text reply before sending media; voice-media duplicate-text suppression stays on the existing path.

A real Feishu repro showed two more gaps. First, dispatcher-backed streaming block replies were being treated as delivered as soon as they were queued. If async channel delivery later failed, the block pipeline could still dedupe the final answer and leave the turn with no visible reply. The core reply path now waits for dispatcher-backed block delivery to settle when streaming callers need an acknowledgement, and the block pipeline aborts on delivery errors so the final payload remains available as fallback.

Second, a live retry hit `Create card request failed with HTTP 400` while starting the Feishu streaming card. That start failure was swallowed by the preview path, leaving no active streaming session while the turn could still complete without a visible final. The Feishu dispatcher now treats streaming start as an explicit success/failure state: partial/reasoning previews only mutate streaming state after a successful start, final text+media falls back to the normal static card/media path after a start failure, block-card replies fall back to static cards if independent block delivery was not actually sent, and late partial snapshots cannot append after a final has been committed.

## User Impact

Feishu replies that combine a text body with an image attachment now preserve both parts of the answer. If streaming close, streaming block delivery, or streaming-card startup fails, OpenClaw keeps or re-enters the final reply path instead of silently deduping the answer away and showing the no-visible-reply fallback.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-pipeline.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` (core 350 tests, Feishu 90 tests)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` (Feishu 90 tests)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts`
