target.title: fix: resolve response prefix template variables in abort replies
target.body:
## Summary

Template variables are not populated when user issues early stop commands. 

- **Problem:** When a user sends a "stop" command (e.g. on WhatsApp), the abort reply displays unresolved template variables: `{model} - {thinkingLevel} 🦞: ⚙️ Agent was aborted.`
- **Why it matters:** The raw `{model}` and `{thinkingLevel}` placeholders leak into user-facing messages, looking broken and confusing.
- **What changed:** `createReplyPrefixContext()` now pre-seeds the `ResponsePrefixContext` with model, provider, and thinkingLevel resolved from config defaults, so early-exit paths like abort have valid values for template interpolation.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** No changes to abort logic, dispatch flow, template resolution engine, or `formatAbortReplyText()`. The `onModelSelected()` callback still overwrites the defaults at runtime during normal replies.

## Change Type (select all)

- [X] Bug fix

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [X] Gateway / orchestration
- [X] Integrations

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #45314

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Abort replies now display the resolved model name and thinking level from config (e.g. `kimi-k2.5 - off 🦞: ⚙️ Agent was aborted.`) instead of literal `{model} - {thinkingLevel}` placeholders.
- Applies to all channels using a `responsePrefix` template with `{model}` or `{thinkingLevel}` variables.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`
- Data access scope changed? `No`

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node 22+ / pnpm
- Model/provider: openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5
- Integration/channel: WhatsApp (reproduces on any channel with `responsePrefix` template)
- Relevant config:
  ```json
  {
    "messages": {
      "responsePrefix": "{model} - {thinkingLevel} 🦞: "
    }
  }
  ```

### Steps

1. Configure a `responsePrefix` with `{model}` and/or `{thinkingLevel}` template variables
2. Start a conversation so the agent is processing
3. Send "stop" or `/stop`

### Expected

- Reply: `kimi-k2.5 - off 🦞: ⚙️ Agent was aborted.`

### Actual

- Reply: `{model} - {thinkingLevel} 🦞: ⚙️ Agent was aborted.`

## Evidence
Before
![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73faefe5-65c3-488d-a429-94edf51ca959)
After
![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e70f899-9353-4679-a63a-4272a8d7d197)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `/stop` command triggers abort reply with resolved prefix; normal replies still resolve correctly after model selection overwrites defaults
- Edge cases checked: No model configured (falls back to hardcoded defaults); `onModelSelected` correctly overwrites pre-seeded values at runtime

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert the single commit
- Files/config to restore: `src/channels/reply-prefix.ts`
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Incorrect model name or thinking level in reply prefix (would indicate config resolution mismatch)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: `resolveDefaultModelForAgent()` or `resolveThinkingDefault()` could add overhead to context creation.
  - Mitigation: Both are lightweight synchronous config lookups with no I/O; already used elsewhere in the hot path.

---

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/channels/reply-prefix.ts` | Pre-seed `ResponsePrefixContext` with default model/provider/thinkingLevel from config |
| `src/channels/reply-prefix.test.ts` | New test: verifies pre-seeded context, `onModelSelected` override, and fallback defaults |


---

## Notes

- This PR is AI-assisted (fully tested: `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` — 919 test files, 2642 tests passing).
- Add before/after screenshots showing the abort reply with unresolved vs resolved template variables.

target.title: feat(slack): support Enterprise Grid org installs
target.body:
Closes #102371

## What Problem This Solves

Slack Enterprise Grid org installations can deliver events for multiple granted workspaces through one bot token. OpenClaw previously compared every event with one startup workspace and used detached clients later, so valid events from other granted workspaces could be rejected or replied to without a durable workspace boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit `enterpriseOrgInstall` Slack account mode. Startup validates the org installation with `auth.test`; each direct `message` or `app_mention` uses Bolt's validated enterprise, app, workspace, and listener-owned `WebClient`; sessions, routes, transcripts, dedupe keys, and Slack caches are workspace-qualified.

Immediate replies reuse the canonical `sendMessageSlack` delivery engine. The listener path must provide the validated event scope and the exact injected Bolt client; a naked client cannot bypass Enterprise admission. The client and `teamId` are snapshotted before the in-memory send queue, queue/thread bookkeeping is workspace-qualified, and the listener client is never serialized or persisted.

Enterprise V1 deliberately fails closed for relay delivery, proactive/deferred/queued delivery, runtime bindings, Slack action tools, and Slack-native approvals. Existing workspace installations keep their current startup, client, action, binding, and delivery behavior.

## User Impact

Enterprise Grid operators can run one org-installed Slack app across every workspace Slack has granted to that installation, while keeping message authorization and runtime state isolated per workspace. Operators enable the mode explicitly and follow the documented Socket Mode or HTTP org-install workflow.

## Evidence

- Added startup identity tests for config/token mismatches, canonical Slack IDs, unsupported policy surfaces, and workspace-mode compatibility.
- Added two-workspace event-scope tests, wrong-app/wrong-enterprise/missing-team rejection, bot-event rejection, and MPDM policy normalization.
- Added listener-client identity and no-network Slack SDK proof that Bolt's team-scoped `WebClient` automatically injects `team_id`.
- Consolidated Enterprise reply coverage onto `sendMessageSlack`: exact-client admission, client/scope mismatch rejection, strict target admission, cross-team queue independence, same-team serialization, mutation-resistant capability snapshots, team-qualified thread participation, chunks/receipts, missing-timestamp rejection, and media caption/upload behavior.
- Existing canonical sender suites continue to cover DNS retry, unfurl policy, identity fallback, metadata, blocks, media, chunking, reconciliation, and receipts.
- Added fail-closed tests for direct sends, actions, native approvals, runtime bindings, live queue admission, queue recovery, and conditional queue transitions.
- Current simplification head `ab49773e556` passes 196 focused Slack tests, Slack package runtime build, repository QA runtime build, focused formatting/lint, docs MDX validation, and an independent security/isolation review with no remaining findings.
- Root extension `tsgo` remains blocked only by unchanged `extensions/qa-lab` Crabline diagnostics outside this PR's changed paths; the Slack package runtime build succeeds.
- The simplification removes the parallel immediate Enterprise sender and its implementation-specific suite: 9 files changed, 518 insertions, 695 deletions (net -177 lines, net -2 files).

Live Enterprise Grid org-install proof (redacted, 2026-07-08 PDT, exact simplification head `ab49773e556`):

```text
gateway:   slack Enterprise Grid org-install mode enabled
gateway:   slack socket mode connected
inbound:   app_mention slack:<workspace-redacted>:channel:<redacted>:user:<redacted>
           -> bot:<redacted> (channel, 145 chars)
request:   Reply in this thread with exactly:
           ENTERPRISE_GRID_OK 20260708-233935-PDT
reply:     ENTERPRISE_GRID_OK 20260708-233935-PDT
```

The request was sent by a human Slack user in a granted Enterprise Grid workspace. The local gateway received it through Socket Mode, preserved the event workspace context, and democlaw posted the exact response in the originating thread. No token, private endpoint, IP address, or internal Slack identifier is included above. This live proof exercised the canonical listener-scoped `sendMessageSlack` path on the exact current head.

Manual verification:

- [x] Validate two workspaces under one enterprise produce distinct scoped clients and session/cache identities.
- [x] Validate wrong enterprise, wrong app, missing workspace, mutable-name policy, and unsupported delivery surfaces fail closed.
- [x] Validate workspace-install behavior remains covered by regression tests.
- [x] Parse and validate least-privilege Enterprise Grid Socket Mode and HTTP manifests.
- [x] Run a live Enterprise Grid org-install message/reply smoke test in an operator-owned workspace.

target.title: security: gateway public network hardening
target.body:
## Summary

Implements comprehensive security hardening for OpenClaw Gateway when exposed to public networks (e.g. `https://openclaw.allegro.earth/`). The existing security mechanisms (non-loopback auth enforcement, auth rate limiting, CORS checks) leave gaps that this PR addresses:

- **IP access control** (allowlist/blocklist with CIDR support) — enforced on both HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrades, loopback always allowed, blocklist takes priority
- **Password/token strength validation** — CRITICAL startup warnings when network-exposed with short tokens (<32 chars) or weak passwords (<12 chars, all-digit/all-letter patterns)
- **TLS enforcement check** — CRITICAL startup warning when network-exposed without TLS and no `terminatedUpstream` declaration
- **Per-IP request rate limiting** — sliding window (default 120 req/min/IP), loopback exempt by default, returns 429 with Retry-After
- **Auth audit logging** — JSONL to `~/.openclaw/logs/gateway-auth.jsonl` with file rotation, records `auth_failure`, `auth_success`, `rate_limited`, `ip_blocked` events
- **Auto HSTS** — `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` set automatically when TLS is enabled
- **Eliminate silent 0.0.0.0 fallback** — `loopback`, `tailnet`, and `custom` bind modes now throw clear errors instead of silently falling back to all-interfaces
- **New security audit checks** — `gateway.no_tls_network_exposed` (critical), `gateway.password_too_short` (critical), `gateway.password_weak_pattern` (warn), `gateway.no_request_rate_limit` (warn), `gateway.auto_bind_fallback` (warn)
- **Enhanced `doctor` warnings** — TLS, password strength, token length, request rate limit checks for network-exposed gateways

### Config additions (`gateway.*`)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `ipAllowlist` | `string[]` | — | CIDR/IP allowlist (loopback always allowed) |
| `ipBlocklist` | `string[]` | — | CIDR/IP blocklist (checked before allowlist) |
| `requestRateLimit.maxRequests` | `number` | 120 | Max requests per IP per window |
| `requestRateLimit.windowMs` | `number` | 60000 | Sliding window duration (ms) |
| `requestRateLimit.exemptLoopback` | `boolean` | true | Skip rate limiting for localhost |
| `tls.terminatedUpstream` | `boolean` | false | Declare TLS terminated by reverse proxy |

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm tsgo` — type check passes
- [x] New unit tests: `ip-access-control.test.ts` (9 tests), `request-rate-limit.test.ts` (7 tests), `auth-audit-log.test.ts` (4 tests), `credential-strength.test.ts` (9 tests)
- [x] Existing tests updated and passing: `server-runtime-config.test.ts`, `doctor-security.test.ts`, `net.test.ts`, `auth.test.ts`, `audit.test.ts` — 245 tests total
- [ ] Manual: start gateway with `bind=lan` and verify startup warnings
- [ ] Manual: test IP blocklist returns 403
- [ ] Manual: test request rate limit returns 429

target.title: fix(gateway): exit 0 on EADDRINUSE when healthy OpenClaw gateway is already running
target.body:
## Problem
When `openclaw gateway run` hits EADDRINUSE, it exits with code 1. Under systemd/launchd with `Restart=on-failure`, this creates a tight crash-loop.

## Root Cause
`GatewayLockError` on port conflict always exited non-zero, even when an already-healthy OpenClaw gateway was listening on that port.

## Fix
On EADDRINUSE, probe the gateway using the correct bind/TLS-aware URL with resolved auth credentials. Exit 0 only when a healthy OpenClaw instance is confirmed. Exit 1 for foreign processes or failed probes.

Probe handles all auth modes:
- **shared-secret** (token/password): forwarded directly
- **trusted-proxy**: synthetic proxy headers derived from config instead of shared-secret credentials
- **TLS with self-signed cert**: fingerprint loaded from `loadGatewayTlsRuntime` and pinned for the probe

Also fixes a pre-existing type error in `src/cli/update-cli.test.ts`.

Supersedes #29499 — thanks @BlueBirdBack for identifying the issue.

---

- [x] Fully tested: VM gates (pnpm build + check + vitest gateway-cli + probe)
- [x] Author understands what the code does
- [x] Codex review findings addressed and resolved

target.title: fix(web-shared): treat exact-limit response reads as complete
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseText` in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts` marks a bounded streamed read as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the response body is exactly `maxBytes` bytes. This produces a false `truncated: true` for exact-size responses, which `web_fetch` surfaces as a user-visible "response body truncated" warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original code at line 275:

```ts
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;
  break;
}
```

When a chunk fills `maxBytes` exactly (e.g. 11 bytes in two chunks "hello" + " world"), the overflow guard on line 262 (`bytesRead + chunk.byteLength > maxBytes`) does not fire, so we reach line 275 with `bytesRead === maxBytes` and `truncated === false`. The `>=` check unconditionally marks this as truncated.

Fix: when `truncated` is already true (trimmed overflow chunk), break immediately. When `bytesRead` hits the limit without overflow, read one more chunk from the stream to confirm whether data was actually omitted.

## Evidence

Two new regression tests in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts`:

1. **Exact-limit read is NOT truncated**: `["hello", " world"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: false, bytesRead: 11 }`, no reader cancellation
2. **More data after exact limit IS truncated**: `["hello", " world", "more data"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: true, bytesRead: 11 }`, reader cancelled

```
✓ does not mark an exact-limit read as truncated
✓ marks as truncated when the next chunk confirms more data after exact limit
```

All 26 tests across all web-shared test suites pass.

## Merge Risk

Low — one targeted change to the boundary condition in the streaming read loop. The overflow-trimming path and the fully-uncapped path are untouched.

target.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** `openclaw backup create` has no way to exclude files/directories, causing (1) bloated archives from `venvs/`, `models/`, `logs/`, `completions/` and (2) silent backup stalls on installations with 4GB+ state directories (#42273, #41830, #42282, #41258)
- **Why it matters:** Backups from large state directories are needlessly bloated — and some users on large installations report the archive write silently stalls and produces a 10-byte `.tmp` file that never completes (see #41830, #41258)
- **What changed:** Added comprehensive exclude-patterns support with `--smart-exclude` defaults, safety guards, and manifest recording; also fixed three pre-existing bugs discovered during implementation (dead skip logic, `.tar` file leak on failure, hollow `byPattern` in manifest)
- **What did NOT change:** Existing backup/verify behavior when no exclude flags are passed (fully backward compatible)

> **Note on GitHub Discussion:** CONTRIBUTING.md recommends opening a Discussion for new features before a PR. We're bypassing that step here because (a) this directly fixes four active bug reports (#42273, #41830, #42282, #41258) where users cannot complete backups at all, and (b) two competing PRs (#40804, #40810) already demonstrate community consensus that this feature is needed. A Discussion would duplicate that existing context.

## Change Type

- [x] Feature
- [x] Bug Fix

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] CLI

## Linked Issues/PRs

- Closes #40786 — Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI
- Fixes #42273 — backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)
- Fixes #41830 — Bug: `openclaw backup create` stalls — produces 10-byte .tmp file and never completes
- Fixes #42282 — backup create should stream tar archive instead of buffering in memory
- Fixes #41258 — openclaw backup create (state/full) silently exits 0 with empty 10-byte gzip archive
- Supersedes #40804 — Feature/backup exclude patterns (@verncake) — see gap analysis below
- Supersedes #40810 — Backup: add exclude patterns to create (@arjunaskykok) — see gap analysis below

## New CLI Flags

| Flag                        | Description                                                                                         |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--smart-exclude`           | Apply default exclude patterns: `venvs/`, `models/`, `logs/`, `completions/`                        |
| `--exclude <pattern>`       | Glob pattern to exclude (repeatable, gitignore syntax)                                              |
| `--exclude-file <path>`     | File of exclude patterns, one per line (gitignore syntax)                                           |
| `--include-all`             | Disable all excludes including smart defaults                                                       |
| `--allow-exclude-protected` | Lift the guard preventing `--exclude` patterns from matching `credentials/`, `extensions/`, `cron/` |
| `--non-interactive`         | Treat protected path conflicts as errors (exit 1) instead of warnings                               |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

### Basic usage

```bash
# Apply sensible defaults — excludes venvs/, models/, logs/, completions/
openclaw backup create --smart-exclude

# Custom patterns
openclaw backup create --exclude "*.log" --exclude "**/__pycache__"

# Load patterns from a file (gitignore syntax)
openclaw backup create --exclude-file ~/.openclaw/.backupignore

# Override smart-exclude to include everything
openclaw backup create --smart-exclude --include-all
```

### Auto-detected `.backupignore`

If `~/.openclaw/.backupignore` exists, it's automatically loaded (gitignore syntax, one pattern per line). Security: group/world-writable files are rejected with a warning. Symlinks are rejected.

### Protected path guards

`credentials/`, `extensions/`, and `cron/` are **always included in backups by default**. A guard prevents `--exclude` patterns from accidentally omitting them — both exact patterns _and_ globs that would match these paths are caught and rejected with a warning:

```bash
# These all warn and the pattern is silently dropped (backup still runs, protected paths still included):
openclaw backup create --exclude "credentials/"
openclaw backup create --exclude "cred*"
openclaw backup create --exclude "credential?"

# Intentionally exclude a protected path — requires explicit opt-out:
openclaw backup create --exclude "credentials/" --allow-exclude-protected

# Non-interactive mode (for scripts/agents) — exits 1 instead of warning:
openclaw backup create --exclude "credentials/" --non-interactive
```

### Manifest recording

Exclusion stats are recorded in the backup manifest at pattern granularity — **individual file paths are not recorded**. This avoids leaking sensitive filenames (e.g. `credentials/slack-oauth-token.json`) to remote backup destinations:

```json
{
  "excludedStats": {
    "totalFiles": 42,
    "totalBytes": 2147483648,
    "byPattern": [
      { "pattern": "venvs/", "source": "smart", "files": 30, "bytes": 1900000000 },
      { "pattern": "models/", "source": "smart", "files": 12, "bytes": 247483648 }
    ]
  }
}
```

> **Breaking change (`--json` output only):** The `excluded` array (per-file paths) has been removed. Consumers of `backup create --json` should read `excludedStats` instead. Archives created without exclude flags are unaffected.

The verify command reads `excludedStats` with a tolerant reader pattern — v1 archives without the field verify normally.

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? **No**
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? **No**
- New/changed network calls? **No**
- Command/tool execution surface changed? **Yes** — New CLI options added
- Data access scope changed? **No**

### Security considerations

| Concern                                                      | Mitigation                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| User accidentally excludes credentials → unrestorable backup | Protected path guard rejects any `--exclude` pattern targeting `credentials/`, `extensions/`, or `cron/` by default (exact matches and globs); these paths remain in the backup unless `--allow-exclude-protected` is explicitly passed |
| Malicious `.backupignore` injected into state dir            | Group/world-writable files are rejected; symlinks are rejected; file must be a regular file ≤1MB                                                                                                                                        |
| Pathological patterns cause ReDoS or filter hangs            | Pattern length (256 char), count (500), and globstar depth (5) limits enforced                                                                                                                                                          |
| Symlink escape via excluded paths                            | `follow: false` in tar options; `ignore` package operates on path strings, not filesystem                                                                                                                                               |
| Filter error silently includes sensitive data                | Fail-closed: any filter error _excludes_ the entry (asymmetric failure prefers safety)                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--exclude-file` pointing to a symlink                       | `lstatSync` detects and rejects symlinked exclude file paths                                                                                                                                                                            |

## Architecture

### New files

| File                                           | Purpose                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/infra/backup-exclude.ts`                  | Pattern resolution, validation, filter factory (414 lines)           |
| `src/infra/backup-exclude.test.ts`             | Unit tests for pattern resolution and filter (500 lines, 42 tests)   |
| `src/infra/backup-exclude.integration.test.ts` | End-to-end archive tests with exclude patterns (562 lines, 15 tests) |

### Modified files

| File                                      | Change                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/infra/backup-create.ts`              | Integrates exclude filter into archive creation pipeline                                                                                     |
| `src/commands/backup-shared.ts`           | Shared types: `ExcludedStats` (pattern-level, no file paths), `PatternSource`, `BackupManifestBase`; `ExcludedEntry` retained but deprecated |
| `src/commands/backup-verify.ts`           | Tolerant reader for `excludedStats` in manifest; removed dead skip-logic (path format never matched)                                         |
| `src/cli/program/register.backup.ts`      | Register new CLI flags                                                                                                                       |
| `src/cli/program/register.backup.test.ts` | CLI forwarding tests                                                                                                                         |

### Pattern matching approach

Uses the [`ignore`](https://github.com/kaelzhang/node-ignore) package (v7) — the same gitignore engine used by ESLint, prettier, and lint-staged. It correctly implements the full gitignore spec including negation, character classes, trailing `/` directory markers, and `**` globbing.

Three-tier matching in the filter (fast → specific):

1. **Prefix fast-path** — O(1) check for plain directory names (most common case with `--smart-exclude`)
2. **`ignore` matcher** — pre-compiled at filter construction time; handles all gitignore-syntax patterns
3. Fail-closed: any error during matching excludes the entry

Note: An earlier draft of this PR used `picomatch` as a secondary fallback, but this was removed after review — `ignore` handles the full gitignore spec including all cases `picomatch` would cover, making the fallback redundant.

### Two-step archive creation

When exclude patterns are active, the archive is created in two steps:

1. Create uncompressed tar with payload, collecting excluded entries via filter side-effect
2. Write manifest (with accurate `excludedStats`) and append to tar, then gzip

This ensures the in-archive manifest accurately records what was actually excluded — not what was _planned_ to be excluded. The no-exclude path remains a single step and is unchanged.

### Post-tar integrity cross-check

Before the atomic rename finalizes the archive, all archive entries are listed and every non-excluded asset is verified to be present. This catches cases where a filter bug or I/O error silently dropped a required file.

## Dependencies

| Package  | Version | Justification                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ignore` | ^7.0.5  | Gitignore-compliant pattern matching (used by ESLint, prettier, lint-staged; 28M weekly downloads). Note: `minimatch` v10.2.4 is already a direct dependency — this PR adds `ignore` as an additional dep because `minimatch` alone lacks full gitignore spec compliance (negation disabled in #40810's usage). |

## Gap Analysis: Why This Supersedes #40804 and #40810

| Feature                                                  | #40804 (@verncake) | #40810 (@arjunaskykok)                      | This PR                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `--exclude` flag                                         | ✅                 | ✅                                          | ✅                          |
| `--exclude-file`                                         | ✅                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| `--smart-exclude` defaults (fixes stall bugs)            | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| `--include-all` override                                 | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| `--allow-exclude-protected`                              | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| `--non-interactive` (agent-friendly)                     | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Protected path guard (exact + glob)                      | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Fail-closed filter (error → exclude)                     | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Symlink protection on exclude-file                       | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Pattern validation (ReDoS prevention)                    | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| `excludedStats` in manifest (no per-file path leakage)   | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |
| Verify tolerant reader (handles missing `excludedStats`) | ❌                 | ❌                                          | ✅                          |

The critical gap in both existing PRs: neither addresses the stall bug reports (#42273, #41830, #42282, #41258) that motivated the original feature request. This PR's `--smart-exclude` flag directly solves them.

## Pre-existing Bugs Fixed

Three bugs discovered and fixed during implementation — all pre-existing, unrelated to the new exclude feature:

| Bug                                 | Location                                                    | Root Cause                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dead skip logic in verify           | `backup-verify.ts`, `backup-create.ts` post-tar cross-check | `excludedPaths` set stored relative paths; `asset.sourcePath` is absolute — `Set.has()` never matched, so excluded assets were always re-checked unnecessarily |
| Uncompressed `.tar` leak on failure | `backup-create.ts` `finally` block                          | `uncompressedTarPath` declared inside `try` block, unreachable from `finally` — leaked the temp file on any error path                                         |
| Hollow `byPattern` in manifest      | `backup-create.ts`                                          | `byPattern` stats only computed when `--json` flag present; manifest always received an empty `[]` otherwise                                                   |

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 6.8.0 (x64)
- Runtime: Node.js 25.6.1

### Steps

```bash
# 1. Create a state dir with large directories
mkdir -p ~/.openclaw/{venvs,models,logs,completions}
dd if=/dev/zero of=~/.openclaw/venvs/large-file bs=1M count=100

# 2. Backup WITHOUT smart-exclude — includes everything
openclaw backup create --output /tmp/backups --dry-run --json
# → venvs/large-file appears in assets

# 3. Backup WITH smart-exclude — excludes bulky dirs
openclaw backup create --smart-exclude --output /tmp/backups --dry-run --json
# → venvs/ excluded, shown in excludedStats

# 4. Full backup with smart-exclude

# → Completes successfully, verify passes

# 5. Custom exclude pattern
openclaw backup create --exclude "*.log" --exclude "**/__pycache__" --output /tmp/backups

# 6. Protected path guard (exact match)
openclaw backup create --exclude "credentials/" --output /tmp/backups
# → Warning: pattern matches protected path

# 7. Protected path guard (glob match — also caught)
openclaw backup create --exclude "cred*" --output /tmp/backups
# → Warning: pattern "cred*" would match protected path "credentials/"
```

- Verified `openclaw backup verify` passes on archives created with exclude patterns

## Compatibility / Migration

- Config/env changes? **No**

target.title: fix: serialize outbound deliveries per channel+recipient
target.body:
## Summary

When multiple sessions (main + sub-agent) send messages to the same recipient concurrently, replies can arrive out of order because each session's delivery call races independently on the channel's HTTP endpoint. Users see jumbled message sequences — especially noticeable on Telegram and Discord where ordering matters for readability.

**Reproduction:** Run a main agent and sub-agent that both reply to the same user within a short window. Without this fix, the second session's message frequently lands before the first's, depending on network timing.

**Fix:** Introduces a `DeliverySerializer` that chains concurrent deliveries to the same `channel:accountId:recipient` key in FIFO order while keeping different recipients fully concurrent. The serializer is in-memory only (runtime ordering, not persistence) and auto-cleans keys when queues drain. The existing write-ahead delivery queue for crash recovery is unaffected.

A follow-up commit wraps `fn()` in `Promise.resolve().then()` so a synchronous throw is converted to a rejection rather than hanging the result promise forever (addresses review feedback).

Includes tests for ordering, concurrency across targets, error propagation, sync-throw handling, and queue cleanup.

Rebased to 2026.3.13.

---

## Real behavior proof — Telegram, live session (2026-05-22)

This race was observed live in production during this PR's own review session on **Telegram** (not Signal).

**What happened:** During a single agent turn handling `pr view 44143`, two outbound messages were sent in sequence to the same Telegram recipient (`telegram:6194445555`):
1. A long ClawSweeper analysis dump (~4KB)
2. A summary message referencing and synthesizing that analysis

**Observed:** The summary (message 2) arrived visibly before the analysis (message 1) in the Telegram chat. The recipient had to read the synthesis before the content it was synthesizing — the exact inversion this PR fixes.

**Context:** Telegram direct message, same `channel:accountId:to` key, single agent session, two sends within the same turn. No sub-agent involved — the race can happen within a single session turn when one send is large enough to lose the HTTP timing race against a smaller follow-up send.

**Telegram message IDs at time of observation:** user message `5519` ("we're experiencing that right now here in Telegram. Look at your last 3 messages"), preceded by the two inverted agent messages. Timestamp: 2026-05-22 ~15:00 EDT.

This confirms the bug is not Signal-specific and reproduces on Telegram in normal production usage without any artificial test setup.

target.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw had local backup export/verify, but no low-friction folder-backed snapshot flow for encrypted backups plus workspace mirroring.
- Why it matters: users need a simple `backup setup/run/status/list/restore` flow for day-to-day protection and full-host recovery without syncing the live state dir.
- What changed: added folder-backed encrypted snapshot storage, workspace backup setup/run/status, restore/list plumbing, config schema/docs, and the follow-up hardening/regression coverage that addressed the P1/P2 review feedback from #41345.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this does not add provider-specific cloud APIs, device-identity export/import, or any live state-dir sync behavior.

## Change Type (select all)

- `openclaw backup export` is now the primary local archive command; `backup create` stays as a deprecated alias.
- `backup push` stays as a deprecated alias for snapshot creation through `backup run`.
- `reset` and `uninstall` now recommend `openclaw backup export`.
- Backup config now supports `backup.target` and `backup.encryption.key` for folder-backed encrypted snapshots.

- Risk: alias compatibility could drift from the primary commands.

target.title: fix(tool-payload): reject oversized XML payloads when text is multibyte
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where plugin/tool-payload callers parsing XML-ish plain-text tool calls could accept serialized parameter blocks that exceeded `maxPayloadBytes` when the payload used multibyte text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The XML-ish parser now measures parameter blocks and cumulative function payloads using UTF-8 byte length, matching the byte-oriented `maxPayloadBytes` contract. The helper keeps the existing fast code-unit rejection path for blocks that are already larger than the limit, and only encodes bounded slices when multibyte text needs byte-accurate accounting.

## User Impact

Oversized model-emitted XML-ish tool-call payloads are rejected consistently for ASCII and multibyte text, so plugin SDK callers do not accept payloads that exceed their configured byte cap.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: XML-ish plain-text tool-call parsing rejects multibyte parameter payloads whose UTF-8 byte length exceeds `maxPayloadBytes` while preserving existing XML payload parsing behavior.
- Current-head proof at `0db0f2b3fbbe5319a3a314e5aae1467be706865c`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts` passed, with 1 test file and 23 tests passing.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` reported no accepted/actionable findings for the final diff.
- Observed result: the regression case with `"é".repeat(20)` has a string length below 64 but a UTF-8 byte length above 64, and `parseStandalonePlainTextToolCallBlocks(..., { maxPayloadBytes: 64 })` returns `null`.

target.title: fix(signal): restore native replies for Signal sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now stay inside the Signal plugin boundary. Direct Signal replies derive the quote author from the normalized Signal target, while group replies persist the inbound Signal sender by account, group conversation, and message timestamp so later durable sends can attach Signal native quote metadata.

The shared outbound/channel/queue/durable `replyToAuthor` plumbing from earlier branch history is not in the current net diff. Raw Signal `replyToId` message-action inputs are handled by Signal's own send-payload preparation hook, matching the provider-owned shape used by channels like Telegram instead of special-casing Signal in shared outbound normalization.

## What Changed

- Signal send paths: message adapter sends, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media now pass `replyToId` into Signal send options and resolve the required Signal quote author locally.
- Signal message action: raw `replyToId` send arguments are converted into durable payload `replyToId` by `extensions/signal/src/message-actions.ts`; canonical `replyTo` still stays on the core path, and existing payload `replyToId` values are preserved.
- Direct Signal targets: phone/UUID direct targets keep their native author value, and username targets serialize quote authors as `u:<name>` for `signal-cli` while preserving OpenClaw's normalized `username:<name>` send target.
- Signal group targets: inbound group messages register sender authors under their message timestamp, including edited messages under `editMessage.targetSentTimestamp` and mention-skipped group messages that still enter pending history.
- Signal reply-author storage: a new bounded Signal-owned cache uses the optional plugin state store when available, falls back to memory when persistent state is unavailable, and is limited to group conversations because direct replies derive their quote author from the target.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal native replies to `signal:+15551234567` and `signal:u:Alice` attach quote metadata with `+15551234567` and `u:alice` quote authors without persistent author lookup.
- Group Signal native replies resolve quote authors from Signal-owned author persistence instead of a shared outbound context field.
- Raw Signal `replyToId` action inputs are prepared in the Signal plugin payload hook; shared outbound normalization has no net Signal-specific change.
- Edited Signal messages register the original target timestamp so replies to edited messages can still quote the author.
- Mention-skipped group messages keep pending-history context and register both the skipped message timestamp and edited target timestamp for later mentioned replies to those ids.
- Persistent reply-author state failures fall back to memory rather than failing inbound handling or reply sends.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

## Verification

Reviewer-checkable behavior on head `6191a5b285d7ddeb7e8072f7efa61a8d48d7b213`:

- PR proof-pack net diff reported base `origin/main 7e0324263b86`, head `6191a5b285d7`, 8 net changed files, all under `extensions/signal/src/**`; `src/infra/outbound/message-action-normalization.ts` and its test remain branch-only churn with no net diff.
- `git diff --check` passed locally.
- Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox `tbx_01kx2g2n6387fvp70y3y31dcwb` (`coral-lobster`) passed `env CI=true corepack pnpm test extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/message-actions.test.ts` with 4 files / 135 tests.
- Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox `tbx_01kx2g2n6387fvp70y3y31dcwb` (`coral-lobster`) passed `env CI=true OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 corepack pnpm check:changed -- extensions/signal/src/message-actions.ts extensions/signal/src/message-actions.test.ts extensions/signal/src/channel.ts extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/reply-authors.ts`.
- `$code-review` closeout passed on this head: model gate passed, native review phase completed clean, and fresh cold review completed clean with no blocking findings.
- ClawSweeper exact-head review marker for `6191a5b285d7ddeb7e8072f7efa61a8d48d7b213` reports no narrow automated repair; remaining items are maintainer acceptance of the Signal-only alias, bounded group sender state, and proof level.

Known proof gap:

Review note: this refresh intentionally keeps the fix Signal-scoped and avoids broader shared channel changes.

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`
- `announceTarget` persists in the subagent registry (JSON + SQLite) so pending completions after restart follow the original routing
- ACP `streamTo` stays separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and never maps to ACP streaming

## Evidence

- New/updated tests: spawn tool schema, spawn registration (incl. thread-bound cases), announce delivery routing (parent `deliver:false`, no channel fallback, idempotent retries), config schema precedence — all pass
- Full local `check:changed` (CI lane, `CI=1`) passes at branch head: lint, prod/test types, boundary guards, import cycles
- `config:docs:gen`/`check` clean; generated config reference updated


### Current-head proof (SHA `368c1f48d14f8b1d0cf0378d227c9d8e639787af`)

Refreshed after the per-agent lookup fix. Redacted terminal transcript posted in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101248#issuecomment-4921711199):

- `routes parent-targeted completions to requester session without channel delivery` — `announceTarget:"parent"` wakes the parent session with `deliver:false`, no channel announce.
- `keeps direct external delivery for dormant completion requesters` / `does not raw-send channel completions` — default `channel` route unchanged.
- Routing + config suite: 348/348 pass at this SHA; `tsgo` core + core-test, import-cycles (0), and `oxlint` (0/0) all green.

target.title: Ensure transcript-to-client delivery consistency for channel-scoped sessions
target.body:
## Summary
Channel-scoped sessions currently have a durable transcript as the source of truth, but delivery to the originating client/channel can drift. In Discord, we sometimes see assistant final replies present in the session transcript / Control UI while the corresponding Discord message is missing.

Because Discord session keys explicitly include the client/channel target, for example `agent:<agentId>:discord:channel:<channelId>[:thread:<threadId>]`, OpenClaw should be able to reconcile whether each transcripted assistant message has been delivered to its expected Discord surface.

## Problem
When delivery fails or silently drops after a model response is written to the transcript:

- Control UI shows the assistant response
- the Discord thread/channel may not show it
- the user cannot tell whether this is generation failure or delivery failure
- there is no durable receipt linking transcript entry -> provider message id
- there is no safe automatic or operator-triggered reconciliation path

This creates session log / client-visible log inconsistency.

## Expected behavior
For channel-scoped sessions, OpenClaw should track delivery state for assistant outputs that are expected to appear in the originating client/channel.

At minimum, operators should be able to tell:

- generated but not delivered
- delivery attempted and failed
- delivered successfully, with provider message id
- redelivered / reconciled

## Proposed shape
Add a delivery receipt / reconciliation layer rather than treating this as cross-client fan-out.

Possible implementation:

- record delivery target metadata for final assistant transcript entries
- record provider message ids on successful sends
- mark delivery status in transcript metadata or a sidecar delivery ledger
- expose delivery state in Control UI/session preview
- add a best-effort reconciler for missing/failed client deliveries
- make re-delivery idempotent using transcript entry id -> provider message id mapping

This should not automatically mirror all client activity across surfaces. The guarantee should apply only to the expected origin delivery target for channel-scoped sessions.

## Related behavior
This is adjacent to, but distinct from:

- multi-surface fan-out issues, where replies from WebChat/Control UI get delivered to another channel
- `sessions_send` internal replies not appearing in a bound Discord worker thread
- Control UI transcript rendering diverging from channel-visible logs

The core issue here is delivery-state drift between the durable transcript and the client-visible log.

## Why this matters
For Discord-first operation, the Discord thread is the user-facing operational log, while Control UI is the canonical transcript viewer. If Discord delivery occasionally drops, the system needs a way to detect and repair that divergence rather than leaving users to manually compare Control UI and Discord.


---

## Current state as of main `e2a4973edf3b` (re-audited 2026-07-09)

Re-audited against source, six weeks after filing. Since then, the delivery queue moved to SQLite (#88665), dead-lettered failures are now retained and surfaced in health (#99842), a channel-final/suppressed transcript marker was added (#100607), and a duplicate-send hardening campaign landed (#96247, #99600, #101024). That work is real but orthogonal — it improves queue durability and prevents *duplicate/replayed* sends; it does not address delivery-state drift between the transcript and the client-visible log.

### Still absent on main

- **No transcript-entry → provider-message-id receipt.** `QueuedDelivery` and the `delivery_queue_entries` SQLite schema have no provider/transcript column (`src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts:79`, `src/infra/state-migrations.ts:1469`). `SessionTranscriptDeliveryMirror.sourceMessageId` is the inbound source id, not the delivered provider id (`src/config/sessions/transcript.ts:39`). Successful sends are deleted on ack (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:142`), so the absence of a queue row cannot distinguish "delivered" from "never sent".
- **No per-entry delivery state.** The only surface is aggregate dead-letter counts in health (`src/commands/health.ts:250`) — failed-only, queue-namespace granularity, with no generated-not-delivered / delivered / redelivered distinction per message or per transcript entry.
- **No origin reconciler.** `reconcileUnknownSend` (`src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts:178`) is queue crash-recovery ("did my in-flight entry land?"), not a transcript-vs-channel reconciler; it cannot detect "transcript entry X was never delivered".
- **Silent drop still reachable with no trace.** The post-send transcript mirror is non-fatal and success-gated (`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts:2358`); queue-bypass/`skipQueue`/best-effort-fallback paths and the crash window between the canonical turn write and enqueue can leave a transcript reply with no pending queue row.

### Scope correction: this is channel-generic, not Discord-specific

The original report framed this around Discord because that is where it was observed. On re-audit, every failure mode above lives in channel-agnostic core (outbound deliver/queue/transcript layers), none in the Discord adapter. The one real per-channel asymmetry cuts the other way: **only Slack implements the `reconcileUnknownSend` capability** (`extensions/slack/src/channel.ts:591`, text-only), so ambiguous post-send rows on Discord and every other channel are currently unreconcilable, and `queuePolicy: "required"` is only satisfiable on Slack today (`src/infra/outbound/message.ts:241`; default is `best_effort` for all channels, `deliver.ts:1344`). The receipt ledger and reconciler should be designed channel-generically, with per-adapter reconciliation capabilities.

### Rescoped ask

1. A durable receipt keyed by transcript entry id → provider message id, recorded on successful send.
2. Per-entry delivery state surfaced in session/Control UI (not just aggregate dead-letter health).
3. An origin-delivery reconciler with transcript-keyed idempotent redelivery, built on per-adapter reconciliation capabilities.

The existing SQLite delivery queue is the right substrate to extend rather than a new sidecar. #87552 remains a narrow, complementary mitigation on the queue side (keeps no-reconciler ambiguous rows recoverable) and does not close this issue.

target.title: fix(gateway): replace ReDoS-vulnerable data URL regex with linear parsing (#102393)
target.body:
Closes #102393

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a model-emitted malformed `data:` image URL containing
repeated semicolons (e.g. `data:image/png;;;...`) would consume 2+ seconds on the
gateway event loop during managed outgoing image preparation. With 40 semicolons
the parser did not return before the 5-second process guard killed the child
process. This is a ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service) vulnerability in
the gateway reply path triggered by `mediaUrl` / `mediaUrls` from model replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced the nested-repeat regex in `parseImageDataUrl` with a linear
first-comma-anchored parser. The original regex `(?:;[^,]*)*` allowed the inner
character class `[^,]*` to consume semicolons, causing the engine to partition
semicolon runs in exponentially many ways before failing on the missing
`;base64,` marker.

The new parser splits at the **first comma** (per RFC 2397: it separates
metadata from payload), then validates that the metadata segment ends with
`;base64` and that the payload contains only valid base64 characters. This
matches the same `indexOf`-based pattern used by 10+ data URL call sites
across the codebase (e.g. `media-core`'s `parseInlineImageDataUrl`) and
correctly rejects malformed inputs where a later `;base64,` marker appears
after payload text.

This is a focused fix: no dependencies were added, no public APIs or config
changed, and all existing error messages and types are preserved.

## User Impact

Gateway operators no longer face event-loop stalls when model replies include
malformed `data:` image URLs. The fix is transparent to all valid data URLs and
has no user-visible behavior change.

## Evidence

### Unit tests — 152 passed across 4 gateway shards

```
 ✓ |gateway-core|   (38 tests) 1188ms
 ✓ |gateway-server| (38 tests) 1039ms
 ✓ |gateway-client| (38 tests) 1186ms
 ✓ |gateway-methods| (38 tests) 1131ms

 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  152 passed (152)
```

Two new regression tests were added:

- `rejects semicolon-heavy malformed data urls in bounded time (ReDoS regression)` —
  rejects a 64-semicolon malformed URL in < 100ms (original: 443ms at 32, >5s at 40)
- `rejects malformed data urls with a later ;base64, marker after a payload comma` —
  rejects `data:image/png;base64,garbage;base64,iVBORw0KGgo=` per Codex review

### Real behavior proof — exercises actual patched createManagedOutgoingImageBlocks

A proof script (`real-behavior-proof.mjs`) imports the actual
`createManagedOutgoingImageBlocks` from the patched source and exercises it
with malformed and valid data URLs. Run with `npx tsx real-behavior-proof.mjs`:

```
=== Real Behavior Proof: ReDoS Fix for #102393 ===
Exercising actual createManagedOutgoingImageBlocks (patched parser)

[  0.70ms] PASS 64   semicolons → Invalid image data URL
[  0.05ms] PASS 128  semicolons → Invalid image data URL
[  0.03ms] PASS 256  semicolons → Invalid image data URL
[  0.02ms] PASS 512  semicolons → Invalid image data URL
[  0.13ms] PASS payload comma before later ;base64, → Invalid image data URL
[   OK  ] PASS valid tiny PNG → 1 block(s), mimeType=image/png

=== 6 passed, 0 failed ===
```

For context, the original regex measured 443ms at 32 semicolons (16× per +4)
and would exceed 5 seconds at 40. The patched parser completes in < 1ms at any
length, including 512 semicolons, and correctly accepts valid image data URLs.


---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.

target.title: fix: keep mapped hook content provenance scoped [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using multiple hook mappings could have a non-Gmail hook treated as Gmail-sourced when the request body included a matching `source` value. That could make external hook content skip the wrapping behavior the operator expected for the actual mapping.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mapped hook provenance now comes from the matched hook path and resolved hook session key instead of a caller-controlled body field. The Gmail path and Gmail-scoped sessions still keep Gmail provenance; unrelated mappings stay classified as webhook content unless their own mapping explicitly opts into unsafe external content.

Maintainer note: Gmail-scoped behavior is now tied to `/hooks/gmail` or `hook:gmail:` session provenance, not body-source-only custom mappings. Custom mappings that only send `source: "gmail"` in the body will be treated as webhook-scoped after this change.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance.

## User Impact

Operators can keep Gmail-specific unsafe external content settings enabled without that setting spilling over to unrelated hook mappings. Existing Gmail hooks and explicit mapping-level unsafe-content configuration continue to work as before.

## Evidence

- AWS Crabbox focused validation on head `74b5c41b3b8b2a442251efca71a3f68496f4d8dd`: `corepack pnpm test src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts`
- Result: `run_9f9f3fc54731`, provider `aws`, lease `cbx_09d75e0f940a`, 50 hook tests passed across the gateway projects.
- Added regression coverage for `/hooks/github` receiving `source: "gmail"` while dispatching with `externalContentSource: "webhook"` and no unsafe-content override.
- AWS Crabbox live Gateway hook POST proof on the same head: `run_1c7045ee011c`, provider `aws`, lease `cbx_09d75e0f940a`, command `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider aws --id cbx_09d75e0f940a --timing-json --script /tmp/openclaw-hook-proof.OD2kCS.sh`.
- Denied/fixed live POST: `POST /hooks/github` with body `source=gmail` returned `200` and dispatched `sourcePath=/hooks/github`, `sessionKey=hook:webhook:github`, `externalContentSource=webhook`, `allowUnsafeExternalContent=null`; no policy call/request/access to Gmail-scoped unsafe-content inheritance occurred.
- Positive live control: `POST /hooks/gmail` returned `200` and dispatched `sourcePath=/hooks/gmail`, `sessionKey=hook:gmail:proof`, `externalContentSource=gmail`; Gmail route/session provenance still works.
- Live proof gap: no external model/provider call was made; the external agent runner boundary was replaced with a recorder so the hook dispatch payload could be shown directly.

target.title: fix(crestodian): run approval-intent classifier on the utilityModel, not flagship (#102360)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Crestodian approval-intent classifier (`classifyCrestodianApprovalIntent`, `src/crestodian/approval-intent.ts`) resolves the completion model **without** `useUtilityModel: true`, so an ambiguous approval reply that reaches the model path runs on the agent's **flagship** model to decide a single approve/decline/other label. It was the only member of the simple-completion family (e.g. `conversation-label-generator.ts`) that omitted the flag, so every ambiguous approval reply is billed at flagship pricing for a fixed ~8-token structured answer. Fixes #102360.

## Why This Change Was Made

A one-word bounded classification is exactly the "utility work" the rest of the family already runs on the configured `utilityModel`. `prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` already supports `useUtilityModel` (resolves `agents.defaults.utilityModel`); the classifier just wasn't passing it. Adding `useUtilityModel: true` aligns it with the family and the cheaper tier.

## User Impact

Operators who configure a distinct `utilityModel` (the intended cheap tier for bounded classification) stop paying flagship pricing for ambiguous approval-flow replies. No behavior change to the classification result — only the model tier that judges it.

## Evidence

Real `classifyCrestodianApprovalIntent` call with an ambiguous message (model path), capturing what model prep receives:
```
before (main):    prepare called with useUtilityModel = undefined   ← flagship
after  (this PR): prepare called with useUtilityModel = true        ← utilityModel
```
Added a regression test asserting `prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` is called with `{ useUtilityModel: true }`. `tsgo:core` 0 errors; `approval-intent.test.ts` green (8 tests: 7 existing + 1 new).

target.title: fix(codex): rotate bounded-turn auth profiles on usage limits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bounded Codex app-server turns (image understanding via the `image` tool, structured extraction, hosted web search) pin every call to the first profile in the auth failover order (`resolveAuthProfileOrder(...)[0]`) and never record usage-limit blocks. When that profile exhausts its Codex subscription quota:

- every bounded turn keeps re-selecting the same blocked profile and fails until the weekly reset, even when other configured profiles still have quota, and
- because the block is never persisted to `usageStats`, the order resolver has no way to learn the profile is unusable and move it behind healthy ones.

Regular chat attempts already handle this (`markCodexAuthProfileBlockedFromRateLimits` + cooldown-aware profile ordering); the bounded-turn path was missing both halves.

We hit this in production: a gateway with two OpenAI profiles (`auth.order: { openai: ["openai:A", "openai:B"] }`) had profile A exhaust its weekly Codex quota. Chat turns kept working on profile B, but every `image` tool call failed for two days straight with `codex/gpt-5.5: You've hit your usage limit. … try again at Jul 11th` while profile B sat idle with quota available.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runBoundedCodexAppServerTurn` now:

1. **Marks the failing profile blocked** when a bounded turn fails with a usage-limit error, using the same `markAuthProfileBlockedUntil` + Codex-advertised reset time mechanism as the chat run-attempt path. The marking happens while the per-attempt client is still open so the failing profile's rate limits can be read, and it trusts rate-limit payloads the same way the chat path does (error payload, or cache updates observed after this turn's `turn/start` began). Callers that don't supply an `authProfileStore` (hosted web search) persist the block through the agent-dir store.
2. **Walks the remaining eligible profiles in failover order** (capped at 3 attempts, sharing one deadline so retries never extend the caller's timeout budget). A caller-pinned profile stays pinned (single attempt, still records the block), and native Codex auth (`homeScope: "user"`) keeps its current single-attempt behavior since no profiles apply there.
3. **Preserves Codex error metadata on bounded-turn failures** (added after ClawSweeper's review): failed `turn/completed` events and `error` notifications now attach the Codex error payload (`data.error` with `codexErrorInfo`) in the same shape as RPC failures, so usage-limit classification does not depend on message text. `usageLimitExceeded` variants whose message never says "usage limit" (workspace credits / spend-cap wording) now rotate and block correctly.

The error surfaced on the final failure is the reset-aware `CodexBoundedTurnUsageLimitError` ("You've reached your Codex subscription usage limit. Next reset …") instead of the raw provider message.

**Stored data model note:** no new persisted schema — the bounded path writes the same `usageStats` fields (`blockedUntil`, `blockedReason`, `blockedSource`, `blockedModel`, `failureCounts`) the chat path already writes via `markAuthProfileBlockedUntil`, and reads go through the existing cooldown-aware order resolver. No migration required.

## User Impact

Multi-profile setups (e.g. a Pro account plus a backup account) no longer lose image understanding, structured extraction, and hosted web search for days when one profile hits its Codex subscription limit — bounded turns fail over to the next profile with quota, and the blocked profile is skipped by ordering everywhere until its advertised reset time. Single-profile setups see no behavior change other than a clearer, reset-aware error message.

## Evidence

### Live before/after proof (real usage-limited account)

Environment: macOS gateway host, auth store with two OpenAI OAuth profiles in `auth.order` (`openai:A` first, `openai:B` second). Profile A's Codex **weekly quota is genuinely exhausted upstream** (resets Jul 11); profile B is healthy. Both runs use the same isolated state dir (`--profile proof`, a copy of the production store with no block markers) and the same tiny local test image, model pinned to `codex/gpt-5.5`.

**Before — openclaw 2026.6.11 release binary (single-profile pin, no rotation):**

```console
$ openclaw --profile proof infer image describe --file test-red.png \
    --model codex/gpt-5.5 --prompt "What color? One word." --json
Error: You've hit your usage limit. Visit https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage
to purchase more credits or try again at Jul 11th, 2026 10:55 AM.
```

**After — this branch (`pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs`), same command, same state:**

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs --profile proof infer image describe --file test-red.png \
    --model codex/gpt-5.5 --prompt "What color is this image? One word." --json --log-level info
[agent/embedded] codex bounded turn hit a usage limit; rotating auth profile
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "image.describe",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "codex",
  "model": "gpt-5.5",
  "attempts": [],
  "outputs": [
    { "path": ".../test-red.png", "text": "Red", "provider": "codex", "model": "gpt-5.5", "kind": "image.description" }
  ]
}
```

The rotation log line is emitted by the new bounded-turn loop after profile A's live usage-limit rejection; the successful describe ran on profile B. Reproduced twice.

**Production incident excerpt (before-fix behavior this PR removes)** — gateway 2026.6.11, every bounded image call for ~2 days (44 failures on the final day), URLs redacted:

```
[tools] image failed: All image models failed (2): codex/gpt-5.5: You've hit your usage limit.
Visit https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage to purchase more credits or try again at
Jul 11th, 2026 10:55 AM. | google/gemini-3-flash-preview: … (429): You exceeded your current quota …
```

### Tests and gates

- New tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/bounded-turn.test.ts` (7) cover: rotation to the next profile on usage limit with `blockedUntil` persisted for the failing profile only; block persistence through the agent-dir store when no `authProfileStore` is supplied; trusting rate-limit updates received during turn start; **failed `turn/completed` usage-limit classification via preserved `codexErrorInfo` when the message contains no "usage limit" text**; pinned-profile behavior (no rotation, block still recorded, reset-aware error); timeout budget shared across rotation attempts; no rotation for non-usage-limit failures.
- `pnpm test:extension codex`: 97 files / 2006 tests pass. `pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass.
- `codex review --base upstream/main` run locally across iterations; earlier findings (persist blocks for store-less callers, trust turn-start rate-limit cache updates, shared timeout budget, preserve failed-turn metadata) each addressed with code + tests.

### Known pre-existing limitation observed while producing the proof (not introduced here)

`markAuthProfileBlockedUntil` persists through the agent-dir store and silently no-ops when the failing profile is only inherited from the main agent's store (its lock updater requires the profile to exist in the agent-local persisted store). The existing chat run-attempt path has the same behavior. In such setups the in-call rotation added here still recovers every bounded turn (the exhausted profile fails fast and the turn proceeds on the next profile); making block persistence work for inherited profiles looks like a separate fix — happy to file a follow-up issue.

commands.author: Jerry-Xin

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```
vitest src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts: 50 pass (incl. dual-mode strict-default + preserveCodeRegions opt-in locks)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass
node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs: OK
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check: OK (baseline regenerated for the additive signature change)
pnpm tsgo:core: clean
git diff --check: clean
```
